# Mcp Connector

## What it is
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard — "the USB-C of AI" — that lets Claude read and act in other systems through a small server you control. It exposes three capabilities: **Tools** (functions Claude calls), **Resources** (read-only data), and **Prompts** (reusable templates). Hosted servers connect by URL; local servers run on your machine.

## Steps
1. **Connect a hosted server:** `claude mcp add -s user --transport http <name> <URL> -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"`; restart and confirm tools appear as `mcp__<name>__<tool>`. (In the app, Add-from-GitHub reads a repo with no terminal.)
2. **Build one — FastMCP (Python 3.10+, stable v1.x):** `pip install mcp`; in `server.py`: `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP` -> `mcp = FastMCP("my-tools")` -> decorate a plain function with `@mcp.tool()` (its docstring + type hints are the interface Claude reads) -> `mcp.run()` to talk over stdio. **Start with one sharp tool.**
3. **Register it:** add the launch command (e.g. `python server.py`) to your MCP config in Claude Desktop/Code; restart. If the tool doesn't appear, it's usually a config typo or a server that failed to start — check the logs.
4. **Choose the transport:** **stdio** for a local server (subprocess, nothing exposed) while developing; **HTTP** for a remote server others reach by URL (brings auth + network security into scope).
5. **Test in plain language** ("look up the customer for jane@acme.com") and watch it pick the right tool; if it hesitates, sharpen the name/docstring, not the code.
6. **Design for the model:** one clear job per tool; precise parameters ("date in YYYY-MM-DD, defaulting to today"); clean structured (JSON/tidy text) results; helpful error messages it can recover from.
7. **Secure it:** least-privilege credentials (read-only where possible); validate/allow-list inputs (never concatenate into a shell/query); human-gate writes/deletes/payments; keep secrets in env vars (never in code or output).
8. **In-app agents:** use the SDK's `create_sdk_mcp_server`. Verify a community MCP's code before connecting.

## Where it fits
Whenever Claude needs to reach into another system to read or act — and the moment you stop being a user and start being a builder.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Reach for `mcp-connector` to wire Claude into a system or to build/publish a connector. Use `git-github` for the GitHub connector/repo workflow specifically; use `managed-agents` when you're configuring which MCP servers a hosted agent may use.

## Honest limits
- Tokens grant real access — an MCP server holds the same power as a person with those credentials; scope them tightly.
- Verify a community MCP's code before connecting; treat every tool argument as untrusted input from a stranger.

## References
- Introduction to MCP — https://claude.com/courses/introduction-to-model-context-protocol
- Official MCP docs & Python SDK — modelcontextprotocol.io · github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk
- GRAPH (codebase memory) — https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp

# Meshy

## What it is
Meshy turns a text description or a single image into a finished, textured 3D model in about a minute — in the browser, no GPU. It then textures (PBR), auto-rigs/animates, optimises, and exports to every major format for games, film, product, AR/VR, and 3D printing.

## Steps (the golden pipeline)
1. Choose the way in: Text-to-3D (from nothing), Image-to-3D (match a reference), or the 3D Agent (chat).
2. Prompt/upload, then set Model Type (Standard vs Low Poly), AI Model (Meshy 6), Pose (A/T for characters), and 2–4 generations.
3. Generate the preview/white mesh; inspect the silhouette BEFORE spending credits on texture.
4. AI Texturing: PBR maps on, Remove Lighting on, pick 2K/4K/8K; Retexture for a new look on the same mesh.
5. (Characters) auto-rig and apply a motion, or export FBX to Mixamo.
6. Export by destination — GLB is the safe default; set a polygon budget for games; STL for printing.

## Where it fits
Fastest path from an idea/photo to a usable 3D asset. Pair with `comfyui` (concept images), game engines (Unity/Unreal), Blender (cleanup), and the book's Section 38 for the full walkthrough.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Reach for `meshy` when the deliverable is a **3D asset** (game, print, AR/VR, render). Use `comfyui` when you only need a 2D concept image, and a game engine or Blender for scene assembly, physics, or heavy retopo/cleanup rather than asset generation.

## Honest limits
- Low Poly is Beta; reflective/glass/hair are hard (use material tricks or Text-to-3D for hair).
- Textures are baked to the model's UVs, not tileable — use Substance/PolyHaven for repeating materials.
- The in-app viewer is real-time WebGL, not a path-traced render; free-plan assets are public (CC BY 4.0).

## References
- meshy.ai · docs.meshy.ai · meshy.ai/tutorials · meshy.ai/3d-glossary

- **Diagnose first.** Text or image? Game, print, or render? That decides every setting.

# N8N Automation

## What it is
n8n is a visual automation platform: drop nodes on a canvas, wire them left to right, and call Claude at exactly the right step. It is the fastest no/low-code way to turn "Claude should do X automatically" into something that runs — trigger to action, with an AI node in the middle.

## Steps
1. **Get n8n and add one credential.** Use n8n Cloud (free trial) to start in minutes, or self-host with Docker/desktop to keep data and keys on your machine (default for client data). In n8n, create a **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your Anthropic key. Every "Ask Claude" node reuses it — never paste the key into a node.
2. **Add a trigger.** A **Webhook** node (method POST, a path like `/ask`) to react to an event, or a **Schedule** node to run on a timer. Copy the test URL for webhooks.
3. **Enrich (Code/HTTP/app node).** Fetch and shape the data the AI needs; use a **Code** node to assemble your fixed instruction + incoming data (`$json.body.…`) into one clean prompt you can inspect.
4. **Ask Claude (HTTP Request node)** — set once, copy forever:
   ```
   Method:  POST
   URL:     https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages
   Auth:    Header Auth credential  (x-api-key = your key)
   Header:  anthropic-version: 2023-06-01
   Body(JSON): { "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5", "max_tokens": 1024,
                 "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "={{ $json.prompt }}" } ] }
   ```
   Tell Claude to reply as strict JSON you can branch on.
5. **Parse (Code node)** — read `$json.content[0].text`; `JSON.parse` it if you asked for JSON.
6. **Route and act (IF + app nodes).** Branch on the result; run reversible actions automatically. **Gate the dangerous verbs — send, pay, post, delete, sign — behind a human** (Recipe 6): approval message (Slack buttons/email link) -> **Wait** node -> IF approved -> act / else stop-and-log.
7. **Import instead of building** (Recipe 7): **Import from File** a `workflow.json` from the n8n Workflows library, attach your Header Auth credential to the Ask-Claude node, replace the `(replace)` NoOp nodes with real app nodes, and read the yellow "Setup — read me" sticky.

Speed tips: **Execute a single node** and **pin** its output to iterate without re-running the whole flow or spending live API calls; add an **Error Trigger** workflow and set **retries** on the HTTP node; use **Haiku** + a tight `max_tokens` for high-volume simple steps; try the **Quik8n** browser extension to scaffold a flow from plain English.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Reach for n8n to **glue apps together with an AI step** — visual, maintainable, event-driven. Choose **Rivet** instead when you want to see/debug the *agent's own logic* as a graph, **LangGraph/Agent SDK** for stateful bespoke agents, and **second-brain** for the RAG API that Recipe 5 calls.

## Where it fits
Connecting apps with AI steps when you want a visual, maintainable flow rather than code.

## Honest limits
- Hosted/rate limits and node quirks; complex, stateful logic still needs care — graduate those to LangGraph or the Agent SDK (Section 12).
- Not a general programming environment.

## References
- n8n docs — https://docs.n8n.io
- Anthropic Messages API — https://docs.anthropic.com
- Ready-made flows in Content Playbook/n8n Workflows (Ready-Made)/
- Quik8n — quik8n.com

## The 7 recipes
1. Hello, Claude  2. Daily Digest  3. Inbox Triage & Draft  4. Lead Qualify & Route  5. Grounded Reply (RAG)  6. Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gate  7. Import the Ready-Made Library.

Pattern to teach: **trigger -> enrich -> decide -> act -> (approve) -> log.**

# Obsidian

## What it is
Obsidian is a free, local knowledge base built on plain Markdown files you fully own — no account, no lock-in. Small notes linked generously become a living graph, and because a vault is just a folder of text files, Claude can read and write it directly.

## Steps
1. **Install and make a vault.** Download from obsidian.md (Mac/Windows/Linux/iOS/Android). Create a **Vault** = a fresh folder on disk. No account needed. This is the same folder you later open in Claude Cowork mode or index with RAG.
2. **Write notes** with `Ctrl/Cmd+N`. One idea per note; a clear, specific title (the title is the note's address). Use Markdown: `# Heading`, `**bold**`, `- bullet`, `> quote` — live preview renders as you type.
3. **Link (the heart of it).** In a note, type `[[` and start a note's name — autocomplete creates a **wikilink**. Link liberally; link to notes that don't exist yet (Obsidian creates them on click). Open the **Backlinks** panel to see everything pointing back.
4. **See the graph.** Open **Graph View** from the left ribbon — dots are notes, lines are links; clusters show your densest topics, lonely dots flag under-developed ideas.
5. **Organise.** `#tags` for status/themes that cut across topics (`#draft`, `#open`); folders lightly, as coarse buckets; a **Map of Content (MOC)** note — a hand-curated index of links — as the main way into a big vault.
6. **Habit + structure.** Enable core **Daily Notes** for frictionless capture; use **Templates** for repeatable note skeletons (matter file, meeting note); **Canvas** as an infinite whiteboard for planning.
7. **Extend with plugins** (Settings -> Community plugins, 2,000+ available): **Dataview** (query notes like a database — "all notes tagged #open"), **Templater** (variables + logic), **Kanban/Calendar** (board and date views). Add only what you'll use.
8. **Sync + back up.** Official **Obsidian Sync** (paid, end-to-end encrypted), or free: put the vault in Dropbox/iCloud/Git — it's just files.
9. **Wire to Claude (the payoff).** Open the vault folder in the Claude desktop app (**Cowork mode**) so Claude reads/writes real notes; point the RAG toolkit's `ingest.py` at the vault for grounded, cited answers; install the official **kepano/obsidian-skills** so Claude writes correct wikilink/frontmatter syntax instead of broken links.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Use **obsidian** for the *store and the manual craft* of notes (vaults, links, plugins, sync). Use **second-brain** when the question is about the *end-to-end AI system* — the CLAUDE.md contract, YAML frontmatter schema, the five build prompts, and RAG-over-your-notes. Obsidian is the map; second-brain is the machine that reads and grows it.

## Where it fits
The durable, queryable store behind an AI second brain (pairs with RAG).

## Honest limits
- Local-first — you manage sync/backup, and edits in two places can conflict.
- Power comes from plugins; keep it lean at first so the setup stays trustworthy.

- Obsidian — https://obsidian.md
- Official Obsidian help — https://help.obsidian.md

# Openclaw

## What it is
OpenClaw is a full self-hosted agent runtime — not a chatbot wrapper. Two cooperating halves: the **Gateway** (a Node.js process on port 18789 owning channels, routing, sessions, tools, and cron) and **Pi**, the Agent Runtime that talks to the model. Everything runs on hardware you control, except the one outbound call to your AI provider (removable with local Ollama).

## Steps (the 8-module arc)
1. **Install as a daemon** (Node 24 recommended, 22.16 min; do **not** `sudo npm install`).
   ```
   curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash        # macOS/Linux
   iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # Windows PowerShell (prefer WSL2)
   openclaw onboard --install-daemon                        # guided setup + launchd/systemd service
   openclaw --version && openclaw doctor && openclaw gateway status
   ```
   Docker path: `docker compose up -d` with volumes mounted for the whole `~/.openclaw` dir (WhatsApp needs persistent state).
2. **Configure** `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (JSON5 — comments/trailing commas allowed; strict validation, hot-reloads on save). Edit directly, or `openclaw config get/set/unset`, or the Control UI Config tab (`openclaw dashboard`). Recover with `openclaw doctor --fix`.
3. **Pick provider + route for cost.** Models use `provider/model` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`, `google/gemini-2.5-flash`, `ollama/llama3.3`). Set a cheap **primary** (Flash) with a **fallbacks** list for auto-failover, and reserve expensive models via `/model Sonnet` mid-chat. Shrink context: `session.reset` daily at a quiet hour, cap `imageMaxDimensionPx` to 800. (Unmanaged spend is the top complaint — routing is ~90% quality at ~10% cost.)
4. **Connect channels.** Set each channel's **dmPolicy** (`pairing` = default/safest, `allowlist`, `open`, `disabled`). Telegram is easiest (bot token from @BotFather, no plugin/QR); WhatsApp = `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/whatsapp` then `openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp` (scan QR, ~60s expiry); Discord needs **Message Content Intent** on. Approve senders: `openclaw pairing list <channel>` / `openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code>`. For multi-channel set `session.dmScope: per-channel-peer`.
5. **Craft the workspace** (`~/.openclaw/workspace`, Markdown loaded every session): **AGENTS.md** (operating instructions — most important), **SOUL.md** (personality/tone), **USER.md** (about you), **IDENTITY.md**, **TOOLS.md**, **HEARTBEAT.md**. File-based memory: `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` daily logs + a curated `MEMORY.md`. Keep files lean (bootstrap truncates at 20k chars/file).
6. **Add ClawHub skills + set tool policies.**
   ```
   clawdhub search "topic"   |   clawdhub install <skill>   |   clawdhub update --all
   ```
   Skills load lazily by description match. Tool policies: **allow / elevated (asks first) / deny**; keep defaults; use `sandbox.mode` for untrusted users.
7. **Automate with cron + heartbeat.** `openclaw cron add` with `--at` (one-shot), `--cron` (5-field), or `--every` (interval); session target `isolated` for most jobs. Heartbeat = ambient pulse reading `HEARTBEAT.md` (keep under ~200 words — it costs tokens every pulse). `openclaw cron list / run <id> / delete <id>`.
8. **Scale (preview):** multi-agent teams + **ACP** (spawn sub-agents, run Claude Code/Codex), companion apps as nodes, reached remotely via **Tailscale**.

Golden first move for any problem: `openclaw doctor --fix`, then `openclaw logs --follow`.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Reach for **openclaw** when the user wants to **own the whole stack** — self-hosted, maximum autonomy, an agent living in their own chat apps. Choose **vellum** for a managed Mac/iPhone "personal intelligence" with Keychain-guarded secrets and more guardrails, and **n8n** when the job is app-to-app automation rather than a conversational agent.

## Where it fits
Owning your agent infrastructure across multiple channels — the open, power-user end of personal agents (self-hosted cousin of Vellum/Hermes).

## Honest limits
- Self-hosting means you own the ops and security (access control, backups, updates).
- Strict config validation: one bad key stops the Gateway — `openclaw doctor` is the recovery tool.
- Verify current install/config/model details against the docs.

- OpenClaw — https://openclaw.ai
- Docs — https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/openclaw
- Repo — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw

# Prompt Engineering

## What it is
A strong prompt has, in order: **Role, Task, Context, Constraints, Format, Examples** — then you iterate. Examples are the biggest quality lever. On the newest models (Fable 5 / Mythos-class) the emphasis shifts: give a clear goal, the reason, explicit boundaries, and a way to verify — then trust the model rather than over-scripting.

## Steps
1. Set the **Role** (who Claude is) and one clear **Task** in the imperative.
2. Paste the **Context** in full; don't allude to it.
3. State **Constraints** (length, tone, must/must-not) and the exact **Format**.
4. Add **1-3 examples** (and a negative one where useful) — the highest-leverage change you can make.
5. For hard tasks, ask it to reason step by step and use **XML tags** to separate parts.
6. **Iterate:** inspect the actual failure mode, then add the *one* constraint or example that fixes it.
7. **On Fable 5 / newest models, tune the scaffolding** (from Anthropic's official guide):
   - **Effort dial** — `high` as default, `xhigh` for the hardest work, `medium/low` for routine; lower effort on Fable 5 often beats `xhigh` on older models. To stop gold-plating at high effort: "Do the simplest thing that works; don't add features, refactors, or abstractions beyond the task; only validate at system boundaries."
   - **Give the reason, not just the request:** "I'm working on [larger task] for [who]. They need [what the output enables]. With that in mind: [request]."
   - **Steer with brief instructions** — one crisp sentence beats a long list; lead with the outcome ("your first sentence answers what happened / what you found").
   - **Ground progress claims** — "audit each claim against a tool result from this session; if something isn't verified, say so" (kills fabricated status).
   - **Prevent early stopping in autonomous runs** — "The user isn't watching; for reversible in-scope actions, proceed without asking. Before ending, check your last paragraph: if it's a plan, a question, or a promise, do that work now."
   - **Give it a memory** (one Markdown file: one lesson per note, one-line summary on top) and **use parallel subagents** for independent subtasks.
   - **Don't ask it to echo its raw reasoning** — that can trip the reasoning-extraction refusal; read the summarized thinking blocks instead.

## Review checklist
Name the objective back in one line; check all six skeleton parts are present; rewrite in the skeleton; show the two changes that matter most. A prompt is done when a competent stranger could run it without a question.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Use **prompt-engineering** to craft or fix the *prompt itself* — wording, structure, examples, effort. Move to **vellum** when you need to *test, version, evaluate, and deploy* prompts as a team behind an endpoint, and to **rivet** when the "prompt" is really a multi-node agent graph.

## Where it fits
Any task where output quality depends on how you ask.

## Honest limits
- Vague format and missing examples cause most failures.
- Prompting doesn't add knowledge — verify facts the model asserts.
- Instructions written for older models are often too prescriptive for Fable 5 and can *lower* quality; strip them back.

## References
- Prompting Claude Fable 5 (official) & Claude 101 — https://claude.com/courses/claude-101
- Anthropic prompt-engineering docs — https://platform.claude.com/docs

# Rivet

## What it is
Rivet is an open-source (MIT) visual AI programming environment from Ironclad. You build an agent as a **node graph** — prompts, model calls, logic, tools — watch it run live, then embed the exact same graph in your app. It sits between n8n (no-code glue) and LangGraph (all code): visual like the former, production-grade like the latter, and its graphs are plain **YAML you can version in git**.

## Steps
1. **Install** the Rivet desktop app from the **Ironclad/rivet GitHub Releases** page (macOS/Windows/Linux); also a VS Code extension. Create a project (holds one or more graphs).
2. **Connect Claude** — Settings -> add your Anthropic API key; set the default model to a Claude model so Chat nodes call Claude.
3. **Learn the ~9 nodes that cover 90%:** Text (prompt/template with `{{variables}}`), Prompt/Assemble (build system+user messages), Chat (calls the LLM), If/Match (branch), Extract JSON, Loop/Array, Object, Code, Subgraph (call another graph as one reusable node).
4. **Build your first graph:**
   ```
   Graph Input (clause) -> Text (prompt template) -> Chat (Claude) -> Graph Output
   ```
   e.g. Text = "Summarise this contract clause in plain English: {{clause}}".
5. **Run and debug** — click **Run**; each node lights up as it processes. Click any node in the **Inspector** to see exactly what went in and came out (prompt, tokens, reply). This live view is the point.
6. **Add real agent logic** — **If/Match** to route on the answer (e.g. GREEN/YELLOW/RED risk), **Loop + tools** for the agent pattern, and **Subgraphs** to extract reusable pieces ("classify clause", "draft redline") — the manager/worker pattern, visually.
7. **Collaborate like code** — save (the graph is YAML), commit to git, review graph changes in a pull request.
8. **Ship it in your app** — same graph, no drift:
   ```
   npm install @ironclad/rivet-node
   import { runGraphInFile } from '@ironclad/rivet-node';
   const result = await runGraphInFile('my-project.rivet-project', {
     graph: 'Summarise Clause', inputs: { clause: theClauseText } });
   ```
   Add **Trivet** tests (input -> expected-output cases run like unit tests) so a prompt tweak can't silently break behaviour. Use **remote debugging** to watch the live graph against production data; clone **Ironclad/rivet-example** for a full worked app.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
| You want to… | Reach for |
|---|---|
| See, debug, and collaborate on an agent's logic, then embed it in a TS/Node app | **Rivet** (this skill) |
| Glue apps together with an AI step, no-code | **n8n** |
| Full programmatic control of state/branching (Python) | **LangGraph** |
| A capable Claude-native agent that owns its own loop, fast | **Claude Agent SDK** |

## Where it fits
When a team needs to reason about an agent visually but ship it as real software — exactly why a contracting company built its legal AI on it.

## Honest limits
- A giant single graph gets hard to read — split into subgraphs early.
- A visual layer — the most complex production agents may still need code (SDK/LangGraph).

- Rivet — https://rivet.ironcladapp.com
- Repo (MIT) — https://github.com/Ironclad/rivet

# Second Brain

## What it is
A second brain is a queryable memory an agent grounds on. The book's core insight: because an Obsidian vault is just a folder of Markdown, Claude (in Cowork or Code) can read, write, search, and link across all of it directly — **no plugins, no vector-database RAG to maintain**. You let the model read and maintain plain Markdown, adding the connections you never had time to make by hand.

## Steps
1. **Capture** notes into a vault (Obsidian/Markdown) — one idea per note.
2. **Drop a `CLAUDE.md` at the vault root** — Claude reads it first every session. It holds your vault overview, folder structure (**PARA**: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive), your note schema, and hard rules (e.g. "never touch Archive", "always link new notes both ways"). This is your contract with the AI.
3. **Add YAML frontmatter to every note** — four fields are enough: `date, tags, status, type`. This turns a loose pile of text into a queryable database ("all notes with status: active and tag: project-alpha").
4. **Install the official Obsidian skills** (`kepano/obsidian-skills`, by Steph Ango) under `.claude/skills` in the vault — they teach Claude correct syntax for wikilinks, frontmatter, bases, json-canvas, and **defuddle** (strip a web page to clean Markdown before saving, cutting token cost sharply).
5. **Drive it with the five outcome prompts** (ask for outcomes, not instructions):
   - "Find the 3 notes this connects to and link them both ways, with a one-line reason each."
   - "Build a Map of Content for [topic] — gather and summarise everything, link the sources, flag disagreements/open questions."
   - "Process my inbox: file each note into the right PARA folder, add missing frontmatter, link it in, and report what you did."
   - "Write this week's synthesis grouped by project — decisions, open questions, new connections — as `YYYY-Www.md`."
   - "What did I decide about [client/contract/idea]? Quote the notes and cite the files."
6. **(Optional) Heavier RAG** when the corpus outgrows direct reading: chunk + embed into a vector store (e.g. **Chroma**), retrieve top-k, answer only from retrieved context with citations. Wire into workflows via the n8n grounded-reply recipe (Recipe 5).

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Use **second-brain** for the *AI system* — the CLAUDE.md contract, frontmatter schema, the five prompts, and RAG. Use **obsidian** for the *store and manual craft* (creating vaults, links, plugins, sync). Reach for the heavier **Chroma/RAG** path only when scale makes direct Markdown reading impractical; most personal vaults never need it.

## Where it fits

# Vellum

## What it is
Vellum (vellum.ai) is a **Personal Intelligence** — an assistant that lives on your Mac (and iPhone) with its own identity, its own email, and the ability to take real actions for you: read and draft mail, manage your calendar, work Slack, triage GitHub, browse the web, write docs, build apps. Unlike a chat window you rent, it runs on your machine (or infrastructure dedicated to you), remembers everything about you, keeps credentials in the **macOS Keychain** (the AI never sees them), and deepens the more you use it. Most people say it clicks after about **three days** (Stranger -> Acquaintance -> Colleague).

## Steps
1. **Install and hatch.** Download the macOS app from **vellum.ai/download** (web works from any browser; iPhone supported, Android/Windows on the roadmap). Create your account and "hatch" your assistant — this creates its identity.
2. **Onboard it.** Tell it who you are, how you write, what you do, and which tools you use — this first context is what turns a stranger into a colleague.
3. **Set autonomy (progressive — widen only as trust grows).** **Strict** (asks before every action), **Conservative** (handles safe stuff itself), **Relaxed** (checks in only for big decisions), **Full access** (complete autonomy). Change it anytime.
4. **Connect your tools** via its **MCP server management** — Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear, and more (OAuth, toggle each on/off) so it works where you already work.
5. **Give it skills.** It ships with **60+ built-in** (summarise-inbox, weekly-report, research-topic, calendar, coding, app-building, image gen…). Add your own by **describing the job** and the assistant writes the skill.
6. **Schedule the safe ones.** Recurring jobs in plain English (a 7am inbox summary, a Monday metrics report) drop a result card in your chat. **Gate anything that sends or pays** for approval; let read-only jobs run freely.
7. **Enable Computer Use only when you say so.** Opt-in; it sees your screen and clicks UI via macOS accessibility/screen-recording permissions, and pauses for approval ("this action only", "allow for 10 minutes", "always allow").
8. **Mind the pricing.** Prepaid **credits** deducted as you go. Watch the **heartbeat** — a background memory/heartbeat system spends credits even when you're not chatting; reduce its frequency, trim memory compaction, or use a cheaper model for background actions.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
| You want… | Reach for |
|---|---|
| A private, persistent assistant with its own identity that acts across your tools and computer | **Vellum** (this skill) |
| The frontier model on demand, no setup | the Claude app |
| Maximum autonomy, self-hosted, fewer guardrails, agent across chat channels | **OpenClaw** |

## Where it fits
For a builder who wants a private, always-on operator they own — rather than a public chatbot.

## Honest limits
- It costs money in the background (the heartbeat) — keep it configured down.
- The relationship takes a few days to become genuinely useful.
- An always-on assistant with tool access is powerful: keep autonomy low and the approval gate on until it has earned trust. Verify plan/credit details before relying on them.

# Vscode

## What it is
VS Code is a free, open-source editor from Microsoft — the most widely used in the world. Worth learning first because **Cursor is built on top of it** (everything carries straight over) and the same skills make **Git** and **Claude Code** feel natural.

## Steps
1. **Install** from code.visualstudio.com (Windows/macOS/Linux). On Windows, tick "Add to PATH" and "Open with Code" if offered.
2. **Learn the five parts:** **Activity Bar** (far left icons: Explorer, Search, Source Control, Run & Debug, Extensions), **Side Bar** (usually the Explorer file list), **Editor** (middle, tabs), **Panel** (bottom: integrated Terminal, Problems, Output — toggle `Ctrl/Cmd+``), **Status Bar** (Git branch, errors, language).
3. **Memorise one shortcut: the Command Palette — `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P`.** Type what you want ("open folder", "format document", "change theme") and run it. When in doubt, open the palette.
4. **Open a folder** (File -> Open Folder) as your **workspace** — always work in a folder, not a lone file, so search, Git, and terminal work.
5. **Create and edit a file** (New File icon, e.g. `hello.py`); type — VS Code auto-detects and highlights the language. Save with `Ctrl/Cmd+S` (a dot on the tab = unsaved). Optionally turn on File -> Auto Save.
6. **Use the integrated terminal** (`Ctrl/Cmd+``) — it opens inside your project folder:
   ```
   python hello.py       # run a Python file
   node app.js           # run a JavaScript file
   git status            # Git works right here
   ```
7. **Install extensions** (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+X`): your language (Python; ESLint for JS), **Prettier** (auto-format), a theme. Reload if prompted.
8. **Source Control (Git, built in):** click the branch icon, review changed files, type a message and click the check to commit; push/pull from the "…" menu or Status Bar.
9. **Run the loop:** create `hello.py` with `print("Hello from VS Code")`, open the terminal, `python hello.py`, see the output. Write -> save -> run — everything else builds on it.

Shortcut kit: `Ctrl/Cmd+P` Quick Open (jump to a file) · `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F` find across project · `Ctrl/Cmd+/` comment line · `Ctrl/Cmd+B` toggle side bar · `Ctrl+K Ctrl+T` pick a theme.

## When to reach for it (and when not)
Use **vscode** to *set up and learn the editor* (panels, terminal, extensions, Git). Graduate to **Cursor** (Section 21) when you want the same editor plus an AI agent that writes/edits code with you, and to **Claude Code** to point Claude at a whole project from the terminal you just learned.

## Where it fits
The default home for writing code and the best beginner on-ramp — the foundation under Cursor, Git, and Claude Code.

## Honest limits
- It's an editor, not a full IDE for every language out of the box — add extensions.
- In restricted/agent contexts, typing into the editor or integrated terminal may be blocked; use a shell (the Bash tool) for commands instead.

## References
- VS Code docs — https://code.visualstudio.com/docs

complete steps, tables, command boxes, analogies, and caveats. Treat it as your authoritative depth. Read it

# ECC Front-End — pinned design system

The Egyptian Cotton Company has **two pinned designs**. Never invent a third or drift tokens. Pick the design the request names (or the obvious one), then build to the **page recipe** exactly — right sections, right order, right count.

Deliverables are **single-file, self-contained HTML** (inline `<style>`, embedded images as WebP data-URIs, CDN fonts only). Vector `<svg>` icons — never emoji. `node --check` every `<script>`, keep tag balance, responsive 380/760/1200, `prefers-reduced-motion` + JS-off fallbacks.

Fonts (Google): **Fraunces** (display serif, weight ~330 for headings, italic for accents), **Archivo** (sans/body), **Space Mono** (labels, formulas).

---

## Design 1 — Green (cotton-science)
Deep-green editorial. Tokens:
```
--bg:#06210d; --bg-800:#0c3417; --txt:#eef3e6; --txt-dim:rgba(238,243,230,.66);
--marker:#d9e02a; --cream:#f2eee2; --ink:#0b2a13; --line:rgba(238,243,230,.14);
--card:rgba(255,255,255,.035); --chip:rgba(238,243,230,.06);
```
Logo: cream. Headline "From ancient to infinity", `infinity` in `--marker`.

## Design 2 — Light (ancient-math)

```
--bg:#f3efe4; --bg-2:#ece6d6; --txt:#14231a; --txt-dim:rgba(20,35,26,.62);
--marker:#c9a24b; --cream:#fbf9f2; --ink:#8a5a1e; --line:rgba(20,35,26,.12);
--card:#fbf9f2; --chip:rgba(20,35,26,.05);
```

Shared: card radius 16px, panel 20px, pills 100px, ease `cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1)`.

---

## Component inventory (class → purpose)
- `.nav` — sticky bar: logo left · centre links (Featured/Topics/Newsletter/Podcast) · right pill (Enter / ▶ Watch intro).
- `.hero .g` — 2-col (1.05fr/.95fr): left = `.badge` (★ + label) → `h1` Fraunces → `.lede` → `.btns` (`.btn--fill` primary + `.btn--ghost` with `.pl` play‑dot) → `.ms` mini-stats; right = `.device`.
- `.device` — rounded cream card: faint cross SVG + `.core` circle with ♀ + four corner `.n` math notations (πi+1=0, ∑1/n²=π²/6, ∇²φ=4πρ, ∞) + 3 accent dots (yellow/red/green).
- `.statrow` — 4-up centred stats (big Fraunces value + caption).

- `.card` — feature: `.ic` marker icon tile + `.tag` + `.fx` formula chip + h3 + p + `.more` link.
- `.stage` — numbered process row: `.no` + title/sub + season chip + mono formula chip; `.body` = detail + 3 `.mini` metrics + dark `.model` card.
- Story card (avatar + name/loc + 2×2 metric grid + italic quote + Implementation line).
- Sustainability stat card (coloured dot + label + big value + caption).
- Research-lab dark card (copy + bullet list + dashboard readout).
- Quote band (large italic Fraunces on a deep panel).
- `.cta` — marker-filled band: h2 + p + two pill buttons.
- `.foot` — logo + copyright line.
- Light-only: `.tl` dated timeline (node + year chip + place chip + side note + h3 + p); `.quote` cards; methods panel.

Play buttons ("Watch Story"/"Watch intro") link to the matching **intro** file; intro **Enter** links back to the site.

## Page recipe — Home, Design 1 (green)
1 nav · 2 hero+device · 3 stat row (4) · 4 head "Ancient wisdom, modern results" + impact panel (12M+ / 2.8B lbs / 30% / φ=1.618) · 5 three solution cards (Crop Yield, Precision Water, Solar Analytics) · 6 head "From ancient mathematics to modern success" + precision panel (2,500+ / 40% / 60 days / 99.7%) · 7 **five lifecycle stages** (Seed Prep → Irrigation → Photosynthesis → Growth Monitoring → Harvest & Quality) · 8 success stories (3) · 9 sustainability (4) · 10 research lab · 11 quote band · 12 CTA · 13 footer.

Optional `‑math` layer: centred warped mesh, φ(x) graph, ∅→∞ (top-right), golden-ratio (top-left), revolving math+hieroglyph symbols, radar sweep blended over the figure, "From ancient to infinity" slogan, members strip. ---
name: "ecc-audit"
description: "Independently audit/validate/QA an Egyptian Cotton Company front-end build against the ecc-frontend design system, the page recipe, and the brief — returns a PASS/FAIL scorecard with prioritized fixes and blocks release on any FAIL. Use after any ECC page/intro is built or edited, or when asked to audit/QA/validate/sign-off an ECC build. Triggers on: audit ECC page, validate the build, QA before ship, does this match the design, sign-off."
---

# ECC Auditor — validate a build before it ships

You are an **independent auditor** (a developer acting as QA), separate from whoever built the page. Your job: prove a build conforms to (1) the pinned `ecc-frontend` design system, (2) the **page recipe** for that page, and (3) the **brief**. You do not fix or rebuild — you grade and return findings. **Any FAIL blocks release.**

## Inputs
- The built file(s).
- The design chosen (Design 1 green / Design 2 light).
- The page recipe (from `ecc-frontend`) for the page in question.
- The original brief / request (every explicit item).

## Process
1. Read the built file. Extract: `<style>` tokens, the section order actually present, every `href`/button target, the `<script>`.
2. Run mechanical checks in the sandbox: `node --check` each script; count `<tag>` vs `</tag>` for `div/section/article/header/footer/nav` and compare to a clean baseline; count embedded `data:image`.
3. Compare section list + order to the recipe. Compare copy to the source.
4. Score each rubric line **PASS / FAIL / N-A** with one line of **evidence** (what you found).

## Rubric (7 gates)
1. **Design system** — tokens equal the chosen design's values (bg, txt, marker, cream, line); Fraunces + Archivo (+ Space Mono) loaded; radii 16/20/100; **vector SVG icons, zero emoji**; light/dark parity where both exist.
2. **Structure** — the sections present, and their order, **match the recipe exactly**; correct count; no missing or extra sections; each section has its required elements.
3. **UX & wiring** — every button/link resolves to a real target (intro↔site play/Enter wired); nav complete; **no dead ends**; keyboard nav; `prefers-reduced-motion` branch; JS-off fallback.
4. **Responsive** — sensible layout at 380 / 760 / 1200 (grids collapse; no overflow).
5. **Content fidelity** — copy matches the source; **labelled placeholders only** where copy was authorised-missing; **no invented** historical/product/material/certification claims.
6. **Technical** — single-file/self-contained; images embedded; `node --check` clean; tag balance matches baseline (a diff vs a known-good backup counts as PASS only if identical).
7. **Brief conformance** — every explicit item in the request is satisfied; list each with ✓/✗.

## Output — scorecard
```
ECC AUDIT — <page> · Design <1|2> · <date>
Result: PASS / FAIL (n gates failed)

1 Design system   PASS/FAIL — evidence
2 Structure       PASS/FAIL — recipe expected [..], found [..]
3 UX & wiring     PASS/FAIL — evidence
4 Responsive      PASS/FAIL — evidence
5 Content         PASS/FAIL — evidence
6 Technical       PASS/FAIL — node --check, tag balance, embeds
7 Brief           PASS/FAIL — item-by-item ✓/✗

Blocking fixes (ordered): 1) … 2) …
Non-blocking polish: …
```

## Rules
- Cite **evidence**, never vibes ("hero has 3 sections after it, recipe wants 4: missing the impact panel" — not "looks incomplete").
- If you cannot verify a gate (e.g. can't render), say so explicitly and mark it **N-A / needs manual check** — do not assume PASS.
- Be terse and honest. A near-miss is a FAIL. Recommend the exact section/token to fix, then hand back to the building unit.

name: "three-directions"
description: "Run the Fish Code Process — the \"options → you choose → build\" gate — for any website section, page, hero, component or surface, INCLUDING existing designs brought in via Fish Code OS (open a Vault project or scan existing HTML into the Studio, then redesign per section). By default before committing, or whenever the user wants to choose between directions. Reads the Resource Board + design registry, confirms intent against the terminology file, checks the Component Registry first, then presents 3 genuinely distinct live side-by-side options, builds the pick, pins it, and registers any reusable block. # Three Directions — the Fish Code Process gate

Never commit to a single design blindly. Build **one section at a time, in order**; for every
section present **3 genuinely distinct, real directions sourced from the Resource Board**; the
Owner picks; then build, validate, pin, log and register the winner.

## Read these first (Fish Code Agentic Workflow folder)
- `FISHCODE-PROCESS.md` — the full process (section order, the section loop, scenario models, engineering hooks).
- `FISHCODE-TERMINOLOGY.md` — the Owner↔agency dictionary. **Confirm intent against it before offering anything.**
- `FISHCODE-COMPONENT-REGISTRY.md` — the house's own built blocks. **Check it first** — a fitting block becomes one of the three directions.
- `RESOURCE-BOARD.md` + `DESIGN-SYSTEMS.md` (vault root) — the Owner's external resources; **the board wins** where they disagree.

## When to run
- The Owner says "let's design/build the X", asks for options/directions/versions, or "which do you prefer".
- **By default before building** any new section, page, hero, component or redesign.
- Also when the Owner brings in an **existing design** — a Vault project or scanned HTML (see below): ingest first, then run the loop per section.
- Skip only if the project `CLAUDE.md` already **pins** that surface, or the Owner says "just build it".

## The loop (once per section)
1. **Frame + confirm.** Restate the request in the house's words; confirm against `FISHCODE-TERMINOLOGY.md` — *"By 'X' you mean Y — confirm?"* For a header menu, settle **content** (items + levels) before **design**.
2. **Source.** Check the Component Registry; then assemble **≥3 directions from different rows** of the Resource Board / registry, each declaring its sources (system · components · icons · type · motion). Free, copyable board resources may be copied (code or prompt) and re-implemented to the project's own tokens — never left as a raw dependency.
3. **Present 3 live options** via the `visualize` `show_widget` tool: labelled `Option A/B/C — «name»`, rendered live side-by-side, one-line verdict each (*signal · win · friction*), one marked **Recommended**. Never decide for the Owner.
4. **Owner picks** (clicks or names it).
5. **Build the winner** to ship standard and run the **harness**: `node --check` every script · tag balance · JS-off render · WCAG AA both themes · responsive 380/760/1200 · single-file · no `.html` links in single-file nav.
6. **Pin + log + register.** Pin the direction (tokens + sources) into the project `CLAUDE.md`; record request/options/pick/provenance in the request log; add any reusable block to `FISHCODE-COMPONENT-REGISTRY.md`; capture any new Owner shorthand in `FISHCODE-TERMINOLOGY.md`.

## Bringing an existing design into the process (Fish Code OS)
The studio tool **`Fish-Code-OS.html`** (Agentic Workflow folder) runs the whole pipeline —
**Sitemap → Wireframe → Design** — on the house design system, with the **Amber ⇄ Basalt** design-system switch in the ribbon. It loads the real vault (`fishcode-wfdata.js`, 103 projects) and the real asset library (`assets/library/manifest.js`). Start from something that already exists two ways:

- **Open a Vault project.** In **Vault**, any of the real projects has **"Open in Studio →"**, which **ingests** its pages and sections (each page → a sitemap node; each section → a recipe block, headings carried as content overrides).
- **Scan existing HTML.** In **Import / Scan** — or the Studio sitemap toolbar's **⌕ Scan HTML** button (also in `Fish-Studio-OS-A-Atlas.html`) — paste a page's HTML. A DOM scan detects **header, nav, hero, sections, footer** and their headings/first paragraph, and builds a Sitemap + Wireframe from them.

After ingest/scan, the detected structure **is** the starting sitemap. Then **run the Three-Directions loop per section** to redesign. Rules that still hold in the Studio's Design stage:

## House drafting format & style (ALL firm work product)
Every agreement, letter and memorandum — **including any external/received draft the firm reviews,

drafter's layout (ALL-CAPS `ARTICLE` headings, lettered `A./B.` recitals, bulleted "-" definitions,

substance, figures and defined meanings; change only drafting and presentation.

House format for agreements (Word `.docx`) — page order is **cover page → navigable Contents → body**:
- **Body:** Arial 11, 1-inch margins, justified. Centered footer `Page X of Y`.
- **Cover page (mandatory for agreements):** a simple, clean first page — **not** animated, decorated or
  "fancy": centered UPPERCASE title, optional one-line subtitle, then the parties (`between … and …`),
  `Dated [Effective Date]` and a `Reference: [•]` line, followed by a page break. No graphics or colour.
- **Table of contents (mandatory for agreements):** a page-numbered Contents page after the cover. Each
  entry is **navigable** — a hyperlink to a bookmark on the corresponding heading (clickable in both Word
  and PDF) — with dot leaders and a right-aligned page number. Give every section heading and annex a
  bookmark (`sec1…`, `annexA…`); build via a two-pass render so page numbers are correct. When resolving
  page numbers, start scanning **after** the Contents page and match the **numbered heading text**, so the
  parser hits the real heading — not the TOC line or an in-body cross-reference.
- **Main heading:** the operative body opens with the agreement's **title as a bold, centered heading**
  (UPPERCASE), plus the optional bold-italic subtitle, immediately before the `This … Agreement is made …`
  opening. Never start the body straight into "This Agreement …" with no heading.
- **Parties:** `This [Agreement] (the "Agreement") is made on [Effective Date] by and between:` then
  numbered parties `1. **Party Name**, [description] … ("Defined Term")`; close with the "Party/Parties"
  line. Identify the correct **contracting entity** — distinguish a client's managing entity from a
  managed vehicle, and add a management/instruction recital where one entity acts for another.
- **Recitals:** head this section with the word **`RECITALS` in capitals, centered and bold**; then short
  recitals — one concise paragraph per bold `WHEREAS,`; keep detailed figures OUT of recitals and put them
  in the operative clauses/schedules; end with a bold `NOW, THEREFORE,`.
- **Deal-specific structuring:** do not reuse a generic clause skeleton unchanged. Tailor the structure to
  the specific transaction and put the **core of the deal — its main pillars, and the purpose and
  structure of the engagement — up front, in a detailed "Purpose and structure" clause**, not buried as a
  lone clause near the boilerplate. If the deal is delivered through subordinate/ancillary agreements,
  describe them there as the operating pillars (lifecycle, what each governs, their status as schedules)
  rather than as a stray "Ancillary agreements" clause at the end.
- **SOW-based structures:** where a master/umbrella agreement governs a relationship, commission each
  project or pillar by a numbered **Statement of Work** (e.g. `LTL-CAT-SOW-001`), each incorporating the
  master; fees live in the SOW. Standing pillars (e.g. an agentic-AI development workflow, or operations &
  maintenance) are drafted as full SOW agreements, not short forms.
- **Clauses:** bold numbered section headings, sub-clauses `1.1`, run-in bold sub-headings, indented
  `(a)/(b)` or `(i)/(ii)`. For significant agreements, make the sub-clauses **explanatory and complete** —
  spell out mechanics, timeframes, procedures and allocation of responsibility.
- **Definitions:** a two-column **Term | Description** table with a dark header row.
- **Schedules/annexes:** `Schedule/Annex N — Title` headings; tabular data as clean tables; all figures
  preserved. A `Form of SOW` annex where the agreement is a framework.
- **Signatures:** `For and on behalf of [Party]` then `Name / Title / Signature / Date` (+ CR No. /
  witnesses / consent blocks where needed).
- **Draft status:** while a document is under review, mark it clearly (e.g. a cover line and running-header
  status `PRE-FINAL DRAFT — FOR OWNER REVIEW · not for execution`); remove the marker only for the final.
- **Titles/naming:** short and descriptive of the legal nature; avoid puffery ("Full", "Master", "Pure",
  "Realization"); do not enumerate conflicting mechanisms in a title.
- **Comprehensiveness:** framework/master and other significant agreements are **comprehensive long-form**
  — model them on the firm's Fulfilment Partnership Agreement standard, with fully specified
  **Intellectual Property** (ownership/assignment of Work Product, moral-rights waiver, work-made-for-hire,
  further assurances, Pre-Existing Materials licence, third-party/open-source and AI-generated material,
  no third-party payments) and full boilerplate (indemnity, liability cap + carve-outs, confidentiality,
  data protection, warranties, term/termination + survival, suspension, force majeure, non-circumvention,
  assignment, entire agreement, variation, severability, counterparts, notices, governing law).

  value and flag it.

# Charter House — Real-Estate Intake & Database Workflow

This skill continues the **Charter House** AI real-estate brokerage project: turning
the flood of Egyptian coastal property material into one clean, trusted, continuously
updated master database, so the brokerage can sell from a proprietary data edge.

Owners: **Ahmed El Gendy** & **Karim El Tarabolsy**. Supply geographies: North Coast
(primary, mostly Ras El Hekma + Marassi), Sinai (incl. Ras Sudr), Red Sea. Buyer
geographies: Egypt, EU, UK, GCC.

## 0. First — load context

The project's source of truth lives in the connected project folder (typically
`…/Charter House Brokerage/…`). Before doing anything, read the two living docs and
skim the database:

1. `CharterHouse_Project_Record.md` — project memory (vision, snapshot, decisions,
   open questions, changelog, **next free IDs** are cross-checked here too).
2. `CharterHouse_Session_Workflow.md` — the operating procedure (this skill mirrors it).
3. **`CharterHouse_AllEgypt_Master_Database.xlsx` — the CANONICAL, authoritative data
   (all regions, 7 tabs).** Every region (North Coast, Sinai, Red Sea, Greater Cairo) lives
   here, distinguished by the **Region** column (Projects col 4; Units have a **Region** column
   at the end). IDs are **global and continuous** across regions (P-###, U-####, DEV-##, SRC-##,
   IN-####).
   **"Update all" = the master PLUS the three region copies** (`_NorthCoast_`, `_RedSea_`,
   `_GreaterCairo_`). The region copies are **kept in sync as filtered slices of the master** —
   ALWAYS edit the master first, then **regenerate the region copies from it** (filter Projects/
   Units by Region; carry the referenced Developers/Sources/IntakeLog; Rentals only in North
   Coast; same global IDs; keep teal headers + white/black data). Never hand-edit a region copy
   directly — it will drift. Deliver and write back **all four** files every time.

If those files are not in the connected folder, ask the user to connect the Charter
House folder (they may keep it in Dropbox). Everything below assumes access via the
device bridge (`device_list_dir` / `device_stage_files` / `device_commit_files`).

## 1. The core loop

```
capture → stage → extract → file into DB → QC → deliver + write back + log
```

New material arrives in the folder, usually grouped **by collector**:
`Ahmed Collected Data/<Project>/…` and `Kareem Collected Data/…`. Rescan the whole
folder (`device_list_dir` recursive) each time — new subfolders and files appear
between sessions.

## 2. Staging (device bridge)

- Stage files with `device_stage_files`; they land under `/mnt/user-data/uploads/…`.
- The bridge transfers **sequentially and times out on big batches**. Stage in small
  groups; stage files >15 MB **one at a time**; retry a timed-out file alone. A 502 is
  retryable — wait and retry.

## 3. Extraction rules

- **Text-based PDFs** (brochures, price schedules): extract embedded text with
  `pymupdf` (`fitz`) — cheap, no vision needed. Dump per-page text and read it.
- **Image-only PDFs / floor plans / site plans / photos / ad screenshots**: render
  pages to JPG (`fitz` at ~140–150 dpi, downscale to ≤2200 px) and read them with the
  Read tool. For many small images, build a **contact sheet** (montage) to read them
  in one shot.
- **Business cards → Sources** (a sales-rep/broker row), *not* projects.
- **`.mp4` videos**: log in IntakeLog, but do **not** attempt data extraction.
- **Arabic + English**: read both; translate as needed.
- **Uncertainty is flagged, never invented**: unknown developer/field → `TBD` and mark
  **CONFIRM**; inferred links → note the inference; register-only pricing → "prices on
  registration"; monthly-only ads → record monthly figure, leave price blank "total TBC".
- **Dedupe before adding**: if a project already exists (same name/developer/zone),
  **enrich the existing row** — do not create a duplicate. Each new file still gets its
  own IntakeLog row.
- **Date-stamp prices.** A price is only meaningful with its issue date. Mark older
  developer/resale schedules as **dated** (e.g. "2020 contract price — re-price before
  quoting"); the EGP has devalued heavily, so old EGP/USD figures mislead.

## 4. Database structure (`CharterHouse_AllEgypt_Master_Database.xlsx`)

7 tabs. **Match existing conventions exactly; never overwrite the auto-formulas.**
**Region** is a first-class column: on **Projects** (col 4) and on **Units** (last column, "Region") —
set it for every new row (North Coast / Sinai / Red Sea / Greater Cairo). **Cell styling: white
background, black text throughout** (bold black headers) — keep it that way; do not reintroduce
fills or coloured text, and when copying row styles make sure you don't propagate a header fill
into data rows.

| Tab | One row per | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ReadMe | — | Holds the **USD/EGP rate** at `ReadMe!$C$23` (currently 49.0). |
| Projects | project / compound | 20 cols: ID, name, developer, region, zone, type, status, delivery, unit types, starting price (EGP), avg price/sqm, DP %, installment yrs, amenities, finishing, source ID, master-plan link, date added, last updated, notes. |
| Units | unit type / specific unit | 20 cols. **Cols K (price/sqm) and L (price USD) are pre-filled formulas in every row — never write to them.** Fill A–J and M–T only. |
| Developers | developer | ID, name, notable projects, HQ, phone, website, notes. |
| Sources | broker / page / sales rep | ID, name, company, role, phone/WhatsApp, platform, projects covered, reliability, last contact, notes. |
| IntakeLog | one captured file | ID, date, platform, caption, file name, project identified, extracted?, linked-to, notes. |
| Rentals | secondary-market owner unit | Karim's owner inventory (mostly Marassi). |

**Auto-formulas (leave intact):** Units `K = =IF(J#="","",IFERROR(J#/F#,""))` (price/sqm,
blanks when no price), `L = =IF(J#="","",IFERROR(J#/ReadMe!$C$23,""))` (USD). If adding
Units rows where the pre-filled K uses the un-guarded `=IFERROR(J#/F#,"")`, replace K on
those rows with the guarded version above so unpriced units read blank, not 0.

**Conventions:** prices as plain EGP numbers; down payment as a **fraction** (5% = 0.05);
"from/starting" noted in Notes; region ∈ {North Coast, Sinai, Red Sea} (Ras Sudr → Sinai);
delivery years as text.

## 5. ID conventions (continuous, never reused)

`P-###` Projects · `U-####` Units · `DEV-##` Developers · `SRC-##` Sources ·
`IN-####` IntakeLog · `R-####` Rentals · `L-#####` Owner Leads (separate PII file).
Every Project/Unit carries its **Source ID**; every IntakeLog row links to the
Project (and Units) it produced plus the file name. **Read the current "Next free IDs"
from the Workflow doc and advance them after each batch.**

## 6. Editing the workbook (openpyxl)

1. Stage the current `.xlsx`, copy it out of the read-only uploads dir to a writable
   path, load with `openpyxl`.
2. Append rows at the next free row per tab; copy cell style from the row above so
   formatting stays consistent. Do not touch Units K/L except the guard fix in §4.
3. Save, then **recalculate** with LibreOffice (`recalc.py output.xlsx 60`) — must report
   `total_errors: 0`. Spot-check that price/sqm and USD pull sensible values and that row
   counts grew by the expected amount.

## 7. Deliver + write back

- `SendUserFile` the updated `.xlsx` and both `.md` docs (short one-line captions) so
  they appear in the chat.
- Use the returned `file_uuid`s with `device_commit_files` to write them **back into the
  connected folder** (same paths, `CharterHouse_Handoff_Package/Charter House/…`), so the
  living files on disk stay current.

## 8. Update the living docs every batch

- **Project Record**: bump version + date; update the **snapshot totals** and project
  table; add a batch block; add new **open questions** (unknown developers, price lists to
  request, dated prices); add a **changelog** entry.
- **Session Workflow**: update **Next free IDs**; note any new folder conventions; add a
  changelog entry.

## 9. Standing cautions

- Karim's owner data holds **personal phone numbers (PII)** — keep the 8,204 Owner Leads
  in the separate `CharterHouse_Owner_Leads_NC.xlsx`, not in the inventory DB, and keep
  outreach consent-aware and on-brand (protects the Charter House name).
- Keep **primary** (developer ads/brochures — Ras El Hekma, New Alamein, etc.) and
  **secondary/resale** (Marassi/Amwaj owner inventory from Karim) tracked distinctly.
- Never quote a dated price as current; obtain a fresh price list first.

## 10. Typical invocation

> "Process the new data in the Charter House folder and update the database, record, and
> workflow." → rescan folder → stage new files → extract → dedupe/enrich + add rows →
> recalc (0 errors) → deliver + write back → update both docs and next-free-IDs.

# EL GENDY GAME STUDIOS — The Game Development Center

An agentic game-development company. One studio, one engine culture, three shipped-and-growing
titles. The user (Ahmed El Gendy) is **Owner & Executive Producer**; every agent below reports,
through their department head, to him. The studio's product is always a playable build the Owner
can open — never a promise.

## §0 · The Three Laws (studio-wide, non-negotiable)

1. **THE ONE-FILE LAW.** Every playable ships as ONE offline HTML file: engines bundled
   (esbuild), fonts/models/textures embedded as base64, no CDN, no network, no
   localStorage/sessionStorage. Build scripts assert these gates and refuse to ship on failure.
2. **THE TEST LAW.** No build reaches the Owner without its Playwright suite green — every
   control mechanically proven (input → state → displacement measured in SIM time, never
   wall-clock; software-GL suites poll, they never fixed-sleep). Every bug fixed becomes a
   permanent check.
3. **THE HONESTY LAW (per title).**
   - *Ages Eternal:* history replayed, never invented; myth labeled myth ("the record seats no
     gods"); readings marked as readings; fiction declared on screen one.
   - *Pawz:* never pay-to-win; Arabic-first (RTL) parity; warmth over slickness; no dark patterns.
   - *Sparrow Chronicles:* the canon-control bible rules; the Forbidden Contradictions list is
     law; tone stays mythic-tender, never snarky, never grimdark.

## §1 · The Portfolio (source-of-truth locations)

| Title | What it is | Canon & code |
|---|---|---|
| **AGES ETERNAL / THE RUNNER / TJARU** | Historic strategy + AC-style hero game on the real record (Thutmose III, Tjaru, Ways of Horus). 2D console → drawn 2D → 3D III·b with KayKit cast, Miu the cat, Anubis judgement, Eyes of Horus. | Dropbox `/The Ultimate Genius AI Historic Council/design-concepts/` + `docs/DECISIONS-AND-BACKLOG.md` (D-28…D-41). Build env: session `~/build` + `~/build/g3` (three@185 + postprocessing + esbuild + KayKit pipeline). |
| **PAWZ ARENA** (the cats game) | The Arena module of the Pawz pet-platform: collectible street-cat battle game, 3D "Lantern Alley" prototype (procedural Persian, gang, rivals). | Dropbox `/Wireframes/Incubator/Pawz/` — `MOTHER.md` (top authority), `PAWZ_PROJECT_RECORD.md`, `ARENA_3D_RECORD.md`, `docs/ARENA_LOGIC.md` (balance truth), smoke test in `tools/`. |
| **THE SPARROW CHRONICLES** (the fairy-tale game) | Mythic fairy-tale of Pearla, the Whispering Forest, the Cave of Pearls and the black pearl; books 1–4 + playable `sparrow-game.html`. | Dropbox `/Wireframes/Incubator/Fairy Tale/` — `sparrow_chronicles_claude_working_bible.md` (canon control), names canon, cowork master, books, maps, art. |

On any task, FIRST load the title's canon files above; NEVER contradict them. Cross-title reuse
is encouraged (the Tjaru g3 engine pipeline is the studio engine), but each title keeps its own
art identity: AUREUM gold/obsidian (Tjaru), Pawz cream/module-accents (Fraunces + Jakarta),
Sparrow mythic-storybook.

## §2 · The Company (departments & agents)

Every agent = one focused subagent run with a written brief and a returned artifact. Department
heads consult each other directly (§3). Names are roles, not people.

**EXECUTIVE**
- **Studio Director / Producer** — turns the Owner's ask into a plan of briefs; owns scope,
  order, and the definition of done; keeps the DECISIONS log; calls the ship.
- **Owner Liaison (NeedHuman)** — the ONLY gate that stops work: irreversible choices, brand or
  canon changes, spending, publishing. Everything else proceeds on best judgment and is logged.

**DESIGN**
- **Game Director (per title)** — holds the fun; approves mechanics against the title's pillars.
- **Level / Mission Designer** — layouts, quests, beats, pacing arcs (largo→presto discipline).
- **Systems & Economy Designer** — combat numbers, progression, collectibles; Pawz Arena balance
  answers to `ARENA_LOGIC.md`; never pay-to-win anywhere.
- **Narrative Lead** — story, dialogue, lore; guards each title's voice and honesty law.

**ART**
- **Art Director** — the per-title identity and its tokens; every surface passes through him.
- **Character Artist** — blueprints (orthographic + rig plan), model selection/retinting
  (KayKit/Quaternius CC0 pipeline), silhouettes readable at forty metres.
- **Environment Artist** — kits of parts (building kit, stall kit), placement plans, light plans.
- **Animator** — clip selection/retargeting (shared skeleton, Mixamo-compatible names), state
  machines (idle/walk/run/jump/roll/attack/hit/death), timing polish.
- **VFX & Lighting Artist** — torch pools, bloom thresholds, particles, tone mapping.

**ENGINEERING**
- **Engine Lead** — the studio pipeline: three (current), pmndrs/postprocessing, esbuild bundling,
  gltf-transform asset surgery, base64 embedding; owns the upgrade tiers (next: Rapier physics,
  three-mesh-bvh climbing, three.quarks VFX, yuka AI, three-pathfinding navmesh).
- **Gameplay Engineer** — controls (layout-independent `e.code` ALWAYS), movement, combat,
  camera (shoulder cam + collision pull-in), interaction; jump buffering + coyote time standard.
- **AI Engineer** — NPC state machines, patrols, vision cones, crowd flow.
- **Tools Engineer** — build scripts with asserted gates, screenshot rigs, debug handles
  (`window.H`), the shrink/embed pipeline.

**QUALITY**
- **QA Lead** — owns the suite; writes a failing check for every reported bug BEFORE the fix;
  sim-time measurement doctrine; runs the full suite before any delivery.
- **Playtest Analyst** — plays the build via the screenshot rig; files what feels wrong, not
  just what breaks (darkness, camera, readability, control feel).

**PUBLISHING**
- **Localization Lead (EN/AR)** — Arabic-first parity for Pawz surfaces; RTL audits.
- **Brand & Marketing** — titles, taglines, store copy, capture reels (GIF/screenshot sets).
- **Archivist** — files every deliverable to the title's Dropbox home, updates the DECISIONS
  log (D-numbers continue), and keeps the intake dossiers current.

## §3 · How the company works (the loop)

1. **INTAKE.** Studio Director restates the Owner's ask in one paragraph + acceptance criteria;
   picks the title; loads its canon; sizes the work (S/M/L).
2. **BRIEFS.** Cuts the work into agent briefs (each: inputs, deliverable, gate). Agents may
   consult each other directly — a Character Artist may ask the Engine Lead about tri budgets
   without going up the chain; consultations are one exchange, logged in one line.
3. **BUILD.** Engineering + Art build on the studio pipeline. Any new library: verify the repo
   live, check the license (MIT/Zlib/Apache/CC0 only), install, and note it in the log.
4. **CHECKUP & VALIDATION (independent).** QA runs/extends the suite; Playtest Analyst reviews
   screenshots; Art Director signs the frames; any FAIL returns to step 3 — a build never ships
   with a known red check.
5. **SHIP.** One file to the Owner (SendUserFile) + screenshots + the log entry (D-number) +
   commit to the title's Dropbox home. Push notification when the Owner is away.
6. **DEBRIEF.** Archivist updates the DECISIONS log with what was learned (traps become rules —
   e.g., "physical lighting ×π", "e.code not e.key", "dunes outside walls").

**NeedHuman escalations (stop and ask):** renaming/rebranding a title; changing canon marked
non-negotiable; real spending or accounts; publishing anywhere public; deleting work; any
choice both irreversible and aesthetic at the identity level.

## §4 · Benchmarks & the elevation ladder

The Owner's stated benchmark is GTA-class feel as a north star. The ladder (per title, in
order, each step shipped and tested): controls that never lie → animation state machines on
real rigs → lighting/post that sets mood → physics-honest movement (Rapier) → traversal
(ledge-grab via three-mesh-bvh) → living AI (yuka + navmesh crowds) → audio → cutscene
grammar. Never skip a rung for a screenshot; every rung ships playable.

## §5 · Session start ritual

On invocation: (1) read the title's canon + latest DECISIONS entries; (2) state the plan in
five lines or fewer; (3) build; (4) test; (5) ship + log. If the ask spans titles, the Studio
Director splits it and runs titles in sequence, engine work first (it serves all three).

# The Official Playlist — Frontend & UI/UX

You are the frontend designer and UI/UX lead for The Official Playlist ecosystem. This skill
carries the design systems already built, the rules that keep them coherent, and the known
defects to fix rather than propagate.

## 0. Read this first — three systems, never mixed

The project runs **three deliberately different design systems**. Never mix their tokens.

| | **STUDIO** | **BLAZE** | **TURBA** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Used by | `1-main-website/` — 24 pages, shared `assets/site.css` + `site.js` | `brand-*.html` — one self-contained file per brand | `Sufi Principles/sufi-principles.html` — music collective, self-contained |
| Role | Company / platform. Trustworthy, editorial, quiet. | Brand expression. Loud, poster-like. | Music division. Ceremonial, warm, rooted. |
| Ground | Warm cream `#F2EDE6` ⇄ charcoal `#2C2E35` | Near-black `#100E0C` + bone `#ECE5D6`, dark-only | Warm near-black earth `#17120B` + bone `#EFE6D3` |
| Accent | **None** — charcoal is the accent | One `--blaze` per brand | Clay `#E07A42` + saffron `#D8A24A` |
| Type | `Jost` — geometric, all-caps, weight 300 | `Fraunces` + `Archivo` | `Amiri` (display) + `Reem Kufi` (Arabic) + `Archivo` (UI) |
| Radius | `0` | `0` | `0` |
| Theme | Light + dark toggle (in-memory) | Dark only | Dark only |
| Signature | Hairline top-borders carry the grid | Marquees, full-bleed accent panels | Arabic-first naming; generative Islamic-star geometry (`geoStar(n)`) |

**The one rule that unifies them:** `--radius: 0`. No rounded corners anywhere, any system.
Circles only for avatars, radio dots, and the success ring.

Full token tables and component inventories:
- `references/studio-system.md`
- `references/blaze-system.md`
- Turba tokens: `--ground #17120B · --raised #221A11 · --bone #EFE6D3 · --dim #BEAF93 · --faint #9A8B6E · --clay #E07A42 · --clay-deep #8f4a24 · --saffron #D8A24A · --on-clay #17120B`. Fonts `--disp Amiri · --kufi Reem Kufi · --ui Archivo`. **Naming law:** every term appears Arabic → transliteration → translation.

## 1. Non-negotiables

1. **Single self-contained file** for micro-sites & Turba: one `<style>`, one `<script>`, vanilla
   JS, no build. The main website is the exception — shared `assets/site.css` + `site.js`.
2. **No browser storage.** No `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`. State lives in JS variables +
   `html[data-theme]`. Playlists, cart and "saved" state are **in-session**; persistence needs a
   real backend — say so, never fake it.
3. **JS-off render pass is mandatory.** Every page readable/navigable with JS disabled.
4. **No `.html` links in navigation** on single-file builds — hash routing (`data-page`/`data-go`,
   `:target` fallback, default `#home`).
5. **`prefers-reduced-motion` respected** on every animation (`.reveal`, marquees, cover breathing,
   EQ bars — all need a reduce branch).
6. Validate after every edit — see §6.

## 2. Known defects — fix, don't propagate

| Token | Context | Ratio | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|--:|---|---|
| `--faint: #9DA29A` | on cream (Studio light) | **2.23:1** | ✗ | Use `#676D64` (4.57:1). Affects all 11px uppercase tracked labels. |
| `--blaze: #DC143C` | Official Playlist accent on black | **3.86:1** | ✗ | Use `#EB284F` (4.54:1). |
| `--ink-dim: #6F685C` | on black (Blaze) | **3.50:1** | ✗ | Lighten toward `#8A8377`+. |

**Passing, leave alone:** bone on black 15.36 · charcoal on cream 11.64 · Ravesion lime 15.87 ·
Radio cyan 10.64 · Podcast amber 10.09 · Turba clay-on-ground and bone-on-ground both clear 4.5:1.

## 3. Brand accents — the registry

Micro-sites inherit the Blaze skeleton and change only `--blaze` / `--blaze-lt` / `--on-blaze*`.

| Brand | `--blaze` | Character | Text on accent |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Official Playlist | `#EB284F` *(was #DC143C)* | Crimson — editorial authority | bone `#ECE5D6` |
| Ravesion | `#B4FF39` | Acid lime — club, floor, night | black `#100E0C` |
| The Official Radio | `#17D4E6` | Cyan — always-on signal | black `#100E0C` |
| The Official Podcast | `#F2B01E` | Amber — warmth, conversation | black `#100E0C` |
| Sufi Principles (TURBA, not Blaze) | `#E07A42` clay | Terracotta — ceremonial, rooted | ground `#17120B` |

**Adding a brand:** pick a hue not within ~40° of an existing accent, verify ≥4.5:1 against the
ground, set text-on-accent to whichever of black/bone clears 4.5:1. Record it here.

## 4. Composition rules

**Studio** — sections `104px 0` (`64px 0` <860px); box-free cards (`border-top:1px`), grids
`gap:1px 48px`; `.eyebrow` (11px, `.34em`) → `h2 clamp(26px,3.4vw,42px)` weight 300; buttons
`.btn-primary`/`.btn-ghost` only; underline-only inputs.

**Blaze** — `Fraunces` display + `Archivo`; deliberate headline line-breaks are content; accent
on one hero element + one CTA + marquee highlights (<~15% viewport); marquees duplicate content
for a seamless `translateX(-50%)`.

**Turba** — `Amiri` display + `Reem Kufi` for Arabic + `Archivo` UI; `.eyebrow` clay; release
covers are `<div data-geo="N">` filled by `geoStar(n)`; owned-track covers are generated as
star **data-URIs**; keep the three-tongue naming.

**All** — nav collapses to a hamburger at **1080px** (CSS `:checked` sibling, survives JS-off);
inline SVG icons `stroke-width:1.4`, 24px in cards.

## 5. UX rules

- **Honest-claim discipline.** No copy implying guaranteed plays; fees cover review time.
- **Honest playback discipline (Turba/any player).** Self-host & stream in full only **owned**
  masters (`full:` → local MP3); **licensed** catalogue streams full **only via the platform**
  (Spotify embed / Web Playback SDK) — never re-host. Label a preview a preview.
- Progressive disclosure in modals; feedback for every action (toast / `.ok-msg` / success ring);
  tabular numerals on figures; visible focus (underline inputs = `border-bottom-color:var(--txt)`);
  touch targets ≥44px.

More: `references/ux-rules.md`

## 6. Validation — run every time

```bash
sed -n '/<script>/,/<\/script>/p' file.html | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/s.js && node --check /tmp/s.js
grep -c '<section' file.html; grep -c '</section>' file.html
grep -n 'localStorage\|sessionStorage' file.html   # must be empty
grep -n 'href="[^#][^"]*\.html"' file.html         # empty on single-file builds
grep -n 'border-radius:[^0]' file.html             # empty (0 or 50% only)
```

Checklist: `node --check` · tag balance · **JS-off render pass** · router ids == view ids · no
storage · every colour pair ≥4.5:1 · reduced-motion branch · 1080/860px behave · no rounded
corners · (players) owned tracks play in full, licensed reach the platform, cart badge hides at 0.
Full procedure: `references/build-checklist.md`

## 7. Extension recipes

- **Add a page (main site):** new file reusing `site.css`+`site.js`; copy nav/footer verbatim; set
  `.active`; add to footer sitemap.
- **Add a view (single-file/Turba):** `<section class="view" id="x" data-title="…">` + `'x'` in
  `pages[]` + nav `data-page="x"`.
- **Add a brand micro-site:** copy the nearest `brand-*.html`, swap the four `--blaze*` tokens,
  rewrite marquee/hero, verify contrast, register in §3.
- **Add a track (Turba player):** push to `TRACKS[]` — owned → `own:true` + `full:` local MP3 +
  a star-cover data-URI; licensed → `prev:` (30s) + platform embed. Reference its id from `LIB`.
- **Add social channels:** append `<a>` to every `.op-social` block (footer + `.contact-social`).

## 8. Streaming & account components (Turba edition — reusable)

From `Sufi Principles/sufi-principles.html`. All self-contained, radius 0, no-storage, JS-off safe.

- **Ultimate mega-header** — `header.nav` · `.nl > .nl-top + .sub`; each `.sub a` = `<b>`title +
  `<small>`desc; `.sub-wide` = 2-col `.sub-cols` + `.sub-feat` "now playing" card; `.scrolled`
  shrink on scroll; animated `::before` underline.
- **Dashboard button** — `.pf-chip` (avatar `#pfchipav` + label + caret; collapses to avatar
  <1080px) → opens `#library`.
- **Cart button** — `.cart-btn` with `#cartn` badge **hidden until `.has`** (count>0); drawer
  `#cart`; global click delegation binds any `.prod-add[data-n][data-p]`.
- **Bespoke media player** — `.mp` (`.mp-now` hero + `.mp-list`). `TRACKS[]` =
  `{id,t,a,al,yr,dur,cov,full,own,lists[]}`. **Preview/Full** (`.mm-b`): owned → bespoke full
  playback; licensed → Spotify embed. Transport prev/−10s/play/+10s/next, seek, volume, spacebar,
  live geometry + EQ. **Platform links** `.mp-plat > .pf-plat`: Spotify · SoundCloud · Beatport ·
  Bandcamp (hrefs set in `paint()`).
- **Multi-playlist** — `LIB[]` = `{id,name,t[]}`; tab switcher `#plsel` + `+ New`; add-to popover
  `.addmenu` per track `+`.
- **Library dashboard** — `#library`: `.profile` + `#pfstats` (playlists · saved · minutes) ·
  `.pl-grid .plc` cards (star cover + play) · create · `.cont-row` continue-listening ·
  `.lib-shop` in-dashboard shop wired to the cart.
- **Footer social row** — `.op-social` (+ `.contact-social`): 7 channels (Instagram · TikTok ·
  YouTube · X · Facebook · Spotify · SoundCloud), `currentColor` + `border:1px solid currentColor`
  so it adapts to each edition; Studio via `site.css`, Blaze/Turba inline.
- **Generative star** — `geoStar(n)` fills every `[data-geo="N"]`; also emitted as data-URI covers.

## 9. Project map

```
The Official Playlist/
├── 1-main-website/          24 pages · STUDIO · shared assets/site.css + site.js
├── 2-brand-sites/           brand micro-sites · BLAZE · self-contained
├── Brands/<Brand>/          organized per-brand copies (sync targets)
├── 3-one-file-preview/      full site as one file
├── 4-strategy-documents/    business/operations plans, profile, T&C
├── 5-alternate-editions/    V2, EDITORIAL
├── Agentic Company/         19 role skill files + org diagram
└── The Official Playlist.md the MUSIC ecosystem record

Sufi Principles/             TURBA edition — full site + brand one-pager + content-writer
  ├── sufi-principles.html   10 views · bespoke player · dashboard · shop
  ├── brand-sufi-principles.html
  ├── Sufi-Principles-SKILL.md · Sufi-Principles-CONTENT-WRITER-SKILL.md
  └── assets/audio/sufi/     owned masters (self-hosted full playback)
```

**Two projects share the folder/name.** The website is the *promotion platform* (Ravesion = its
promo vertical). `The Official Playlist.md` is the *music label ecosystem* (Sufi Principles is a
music-division collective, TURBA edition). Same family, different entities — never merge naming.
