--- name: "social-post-carousel-design" description: "Build animated social-media posts and Instagram carousels in the approved house style: emerald-on-warm-paper design system, Space Mono throughout, dot-grid texture, badged vector icons, animated node-and-arrow workflow diagrams, an IDE-style typed code block, and the house motion (typewriter headline + fade-rise \"appears\" body + live-colour typed code + looping workflow flow). Delivers individual 1080×1350 posts plus one swipeable all-in-one carousel, branded someone.lawyer. Use for any social post/carousel, post generator, \"make it different from the source\", agent-pattern explainers, or animating a post. Triggers on: social post, Instagram carousel, post design, carousel slides, animate the post, typewriter, IDE code, animated workflow/diagram, eight agent types." --- # Social Post & Carousel Design — house system (approved) Reproducible spec for Ahmed's approved social posts. Every post is one self-contained HTML file at **1080×1350**. A multi-slide set ships as individual post files **plus one swipeable all-in-one carousel**. Build with a small Python generator that emits the HTML, then **render-verify in the browser** (fit ≤ 1350, fonts loaded, nothing clipped) before delivering. Brand = **someone.lawyer**. Preferred build: a Python script that defines the shared CSS once, a data list of slides, per-slide render functions, and a combined-viewer template — emit files into the project/Design-Bank folder. ## 1. Canvas & layout skeleton ```css .stage{width:1080px;height:1350px;position:relative;overflow:hidden;background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink); font-family:'Space Mono',monospace; background-image:radial-gradient(var(--grid) 1.6px,transparent 1.6px);background-size:34px 34px} .glow{position:absolute;top:-160px;right:-120px;width:620px;height:620px;pointer-events:none; background:radial-gradient(circle,rgba(14,122,99,.14),transparent 66%)} .pad{position:absolute;inset:0;padding:78px 80px 70px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;z-index:2} .pad>*{flex:none} /* nothing shrinks */ .spacer{flex:1;min-height:0} /* pins footer to bottom */ ``` Slide markup: `
…blocks…
FOOTER
`. **Fit discipline:** after render, `document.querySelector('.pad').scrollHeight` MUST be ≤ 1350. If it overflows, shrink type/margins — never clip. ## 2. Design tokens (the approved emerald-on-warm-paper palette) ```css :root{ --bg:#FBFAF6; --ink:#182420; --muted:#68706A; --mut2:#AEB6AE; --accent:#0E7A63; --accent2:#12987C; --pill:#E4F1EC; --pillbd:#C7E4DA; --card:#F3F1EA; --line:#E6E2D8; --line2:#D6DAD2; --grid:#DDD8CB; --cardbd:#E6E2D8; } html,body{background:#c7c4bb;font-family:'Space Mono',monospace} ``` One accent (emerald) used throughout: pills, dots, connectors, callout bar, icon badges. Warn/amber accent only for "Watch-out": bg `#F6ECE2`, color `#B4692B`. ## 3. Typography — Space Mono EVERYWHERE Load `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Space+Mono:wght@400;700&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700;800&display=swap')`. Body, headings, labels, footer — all **Space Mono** (never Arial/Times/Inter as the visible face). Set the base font on **both `html,body` and `.stage`** (the carousel slides aren't wrapped in `.stage`, so `html,body` must carry it or body text falls back to Times). - Title `h1`: Space Mono 700, 70px (`.sm` 60px), line-height 1.04, letter-spacing −1.5px. - Eyebrow/label/tag/brand/footer: Space Mono 700, uppercase, letter-spacing ~.14–.16em. ## 4. Component anatomy (exact) Header (`.head` space-between): left `.eyebrow` = `NN / NN · SECTION` (accent "/" and "·" via `.dot`); right `.brand` pill = the handle. ```css .eyebrow{font-weight:700;font-size:23px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink)} .eyebrow .dot{color:var(--accent);margin:0 10px} .brand{font-weight:700;font-size:21px;letter-spacing:.14em;color:var(--accent);background:var(--pill);border:1.5px solid var(--pillbd);border-radius:12px;padding:11px 18px} ``` Title row (`.titlerow` margin-top 40): `

` + inline `.tag` pill (`font-size:18px;color:var(--accent);background:var(--pill);border-radius:9px;padding:9px 14px;text-transform:uppercase`). Lede: `font-size:26–27px;line-height:1.44;color:#28242F;margin-top:24px;max-width:920px`; bold key phrase `.lede b{color:var(--ink)}`. Comparison columns `.cols` (2-col grid, gap 26): each `.col{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--cardbd);border-radius:22px;padding:34px}`; header `.colh` is flex with a 26px inline icon — left column ink, right column accent; bullet rows `.li` with an 11px accent dot. Accent-bar callout: `.callout{background:#E9F3EF;border-left:7px solid var(--accent);border-radius:14px;padding:26px 32px;font-size:25px;font-weight:700;color:var(--ink)}` (`.callout b{color:var(--accent)}`); centered `.quote` variant for closers. Chip grid `.chips` (2-col): `.chip{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--cardbd);border-radius:16px;padding:22px 26px;display:flex;gap:18px}` with a 46px rounded **icon badge** `.cci{background:var(--pill);color:var(--accent)}`. **"In practice" module** (fills empty space, adds teaching): a `.slabel` "IN PRACTICE" (accent, uppercase, letter-spacing .16em) → `.example` (spark icon + one concrete example line) → two `.crow` rows: **Strength** (check icon, accent badge) and **Watch-out** (alert icon, `.crow.warn` amber badge). Each `.crow{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--cardbd);border-radius:16px;padding:20px 26px;gap:18px}`, badge 48px, text 23px with bold accent-ink label. Footer: hairline `border-top:1px solid var(--line)`; left `.fa` = `@someone.lawyer` (bold), right `.fb` = `someone.lawyer` (muted `#ADA99C`). ## 5. Icons & spot illustrations Inline SVG only (stroke, `currentColor`), each in a rounded tinted badge (`background:var(--pill);color:var(--accent)`). Give comparison headers small icons. Include ≥1 **spot illustration** where space allows (e.g. a fork: input dot → decision diamond → two labelled badges "Workflow / you set the path" and "Agent / model picks the path"), drawn in CSS-var colours. ## 6. IDE code block (for code slides) Render code as a mini dark IDE, not a plain `
`:
- Title bar `.ide-bar{background:#132420}` with three traffic-light dots (`#EC6A5E`,`#F4BF4F`,`#61C554`) + filename (e.g. `matter_graph.py`).
- Body `.ide-body{background:#0F1B18;display:flex}`: a right-aligned line-number `.gutter` (`color:#3E524B`, divider `#1D2E29`) + `.code2`.
- Dark syntax: keyword `#6FD3B0`, type `#E0A356`, string `#9BD17E`, comment `#6E7E76`, fn `#7FB7F0`, text `#D7E2DB`. Font Space Mono ~19–20px. Keep short enough to fit.

## 7. Diagram library (animated node-and-arrow)
Diagrams are the hero of explainer slides. Helpers (SVG viewBox `0 0 900 H`, rendered `width:100%`):
- `node(x,y,w,h,label)` = rounded rect `fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--accent)` + centred Space Mono label.
- `conn(d)` = ``; muted variant uses `var(--mut2)`/`#ahm`; bidirectional adds `marker-start="url(#ahs)"`.
- One `` with arrow markers `ah`/`ahm`/`ahs` per svg.
The eight agent-pattern diagrams (each its own slide): **Sequential** (in → Step1→2→3 → out), **Parallel** (in fans to Worker A/B/C then merges to out), **Routing** (in → Router → one of three paths; chosen path accent, others `--mut2`/`--line2`), **Orchestrator** (Orchestrator dispatches down to 3 Workers), **Evaluator Loop** (Generate→Evaluate→pass, plus a "retry" arc back to Generate), **Tool Loop** (Agent → Tool "call", Tool → Agent "result", Tool → done), **Supervisor** (Supervisor ⇄ 3 Agents, two-way markers), **Network** (5 Agent nodes in a mesh of interconnections).

## 8. Animation rules (apply on carousel slides; keep standalone exports static)
Scope motion to `.slide.on …`. Re-trigger on every slide change.
**(a) "Appears"** for every `.pad` child — staggered fade + rise + blur/scale settle:
```css
.slide .pad>*{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px) scale(.985);filter:blur(6px)}
.slide.on .pad>*{animation:rise 1.5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both}
.slide.on .pad>*:nth-child(1){animation-delay:.10s} /* …step .16s per child, up to nth-child(11) */
.slide.on .pad>*.hold{animation:none}   /* held elements wait */
@keyframes rise{0%{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px) scale(.985);filter:blur(6px)}60%{filter:blur(0)}100%{opacity:1;transform:none;filter:blur(0)}}
```
**(b) Typewriter headline** (slow, ~70–90 ms/char, blinking accent caret):
```js
function typeTitle(sl){var h=sl.querySelector('h1');if(!h)return;if(!h.dataset.full)h.dataset.full=h.textContent;var f=h.dataset.full;if(h._t)clearInterval(h._t);h.textContent='';h.classList.add('caret');var i=0;h._t=setInterval(function(){i++;h.textContent=f.slice(0,i);if(i>=f.length){clearInterval(h._t);setTimeout(function(){h.classList.remove('caret');},700);}},70);}
```
`h1.caret::after{content:'';display:inline-block;width:.55ch;height:.9em;background:var(--accent);margin-left:8px;animation:blink .78s steps(1) infinite}` `@keyframes blink{50%{opacity:0}}`.
**(c) Typed code WITH live colours** — reveal the already-highlighted code token-by-token (never plain-then-swap). Parse `.code2` childNodes once into `{cls,text}` tokens, then rebuild char-by-char (~22 ms/char, one char per tick) preserving span classes; caret trails.
```js
function renderTokens(el,tok,count){el.textContent='';var n=0;for(var k=0;k=code._len){clearInterval(code._t);code.classList.remove('caret');code.innerHTML=code._full;if(done)done();}},22);}
```
**(d) Hold-then-reveal:** on a code slide, everything AFTER the IDE stays hidden (add class `hold`) while the code types; on the code's done callback, reveal those siblings one by one (remove `hold`, set inline `animation:'rise 1.2s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both'` with staggered `animationDelay`). Clear inline animation before re-holding on revisit.
**(e) Looping workflow flow** (not a one-shot draw — keeps replaying):
```css
.dg .ln,.illo .ln{stroke-dasharray:11 13;animation:flow 1.7s linear infinite}
@keyframes flow{to{stroke-dashoffset:-24}}
```
`typeSlide(sl)` orchestrates b→c→d on activation; title types first, then code, then the held rows reveal.

## 9. Combined carousel (all-in-one deliverable)
One HTML: each slide is `
` inside `.board{width:1080px;height:1350px;transform-origin:center}`. A `fit()` scales the board to the viewport (`transform:scale(min(vw/1080,vh/1350))`), on load + resize. Nav bar: prev/next arrows, dots, `n / N` counter, keyboard ←/→, touch-swipe. `go(i)` toggles `.on` and calls `typeSlide(slides[i])`; call `typeSlide(slides[0])` at load. `.slide{position:absolute;inset:0;opacity:0;transition:opacity .45s}` `.slide.on{opacity:1}`.

## 10. Diverge-from-source
When basing a design on a reference (e.g. the PRACTICAI indigo deck): match its **anatomy/structure** but change palette (→ this emerald/warm system), background texture (→ dot grid), and keep the layout discipline — so it reads as its own brand, never a lookalike.

## 11. Delivery
Save individual posts + the combined carousel into the project/Design-Bank folder; present the combined carousel as the primary deliverable. Offer flat-PNG export if the client needs upload-ready images. Always render-verify first (see `visual-self-verify`). Screenshots can time out even when the DOM is fine — also confirm structurally via `javascript_tool` (padScroll, computed font-family = Space Mono).

name: "ultimate-frontend-uiux"
description: "The one powerful web-design skill for building, reviewing, upgrading, or redesigning ANY website, page, section, component, UI or UX. Award-winning anti-slop standard (Design Read + 3 dials, typography/colour/layout discipline, motion honesty, a Pre-Flight ship gate, a PARITY GATE) plus a Design-System & Resource Arsenal (70+ design systems, component/motion/icon/type/colour/texture libraries + 3D) — pulls from MULTIPLE systems, never defaults to one. For social posts and Instagram carousels, defer to the dedicated social-post-carousel-design skill. Triggers on: build/redesign/upgrade a site, page, hero, section, component, comparison, pricing, cards, UI pass, UX review, choose a design system, pull components, \"make it award-winning / professional / not basic / not AI-default / not slop\"."
---

# Ultimate Front-End & UI/UX — the one powerful web-design skill
Craft + governance (Taste-merged) **and** a full design-system & resource arsenal. Senior agency product designer + FE engineer. Everything is client-grade, award-worthy, anti-slop. "Basic / AI-default / slop" is a failure.

> **Merge note.** Folds in Taste Skill's transferable directives (leonxlnx/taste-skill, MIT), translated to the single-file vanilla vault; its React/Tailwind/Motion/GSAP + "install an icon library / picsum" rules are adapted or dropped where they conflict with self-containment. **Taste Skill is now merged here — do not run it stacked as a second skill** (board rule #1 is thereby resolved).

## 0. The bar
Would this win an Awwwards mention? If not it isn't done. Every component = the best real version on the internet. Varied section archetypes, never one repeated layout. Ship must pass **Pre-Flight (§12)**.

## 0.5 Design Read (first, always)
One line: *register* (institutional/editorial/technical/luxury/playful) · *audience* · *the ONE job of the page*. Ambiguous → ask ONE question. **Anti-default discipline:** name the templated AI reach for this brief and avoid it.

## 0.6 Three dials (drive layout/motion/spacing)
DESIGN_VARIANCE (symmetric→experimental) · MOTION_INTENSITY (static→cinematic) · VISUAL_DENSITY (airy→dense). Infer, state, obey.

## 0.7 RENDER GATE — self-verify before you show (MANDATORY)
You cannot trust un-rendered markup. Before presenting ANY visual (page, post, carousel slide, component) you MUST render it, look at it with your own eyes, and fix what you see. Shipping a layout you never rendered is the #1 failure and is banned.
- **How (sandbox has no headless browser — Chromium download is blocked, playwright deps fail):** use the user's connected Chrome. `list_connected_browsers` → create/navigate a tab → inject → screenshot. The navigate tool rejects long `data:`/`file://` URLs, so inject via `javascript_tool`: navigate the tab to `https://example.com`, base64 the HTML in the shell, and decode in-page — `var bin=atob(b64);var bytes=Uint8Array.from(bin,c=>c.charCodeAt(0));var html=new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes);document.open();document.write(html);document.close();`. Then set `document.documentElement.style.zoom` (~0.5) or scale the stage so a full fixed-size canvas (e.g. 1080×1350) fits one screenshot. `computer{screenshot}` (retry once if the renderer times out — screenshots can time out even when the DOM is fine, so also verify structurally by reading `.pad`/board scrollHeight via `javascript_tool`), then `computer{zoom, region:[x0,y0,x1,y1]}` into areas to check detail. Close the tab when done. For animated posts render the STATIC final frame since one frame can't show motion.
- **Check every time:** content fills the canvas (no dead zone, nothing floating in a void) · nothing overflows or overlaps · connectors/arrows land where intended · text not clipped · icons/illustrations actually render · contrast holds. Iterate render → fix → render until clean.
- **Only present after it passes.** See the standalone `visual-self-verify` skill for the full loop.

> **Social posts & carousels →** For Instagram/social posts and multi-slide carousels (individual 1080×1350 posts **plus one swipeable all-in-one carousel**, badged vector icons, a spot illustration, an IDE-style code block, and the house **animation rules** — a typewriter headline + an "appears" fade-rise body, typed code, and looping animated workflow diagrams that keep replaying), use the dedicated **`social-post-carousel-design`** skill. Body/headline default font follows the reference header face (house default **Space Mono**, never Arial/Times). Recreate a reference by matching its anatomy but diverging on palette, texture and display face so it reads as its own brand.

## 1. Before you build
Load design system + component library (`_COMPONENT-LIBRARY.md`) → pull from the **Arsenal (§17)**, re-implement to project tokens → read target tokens → define SCOPE (§13).

## 2. Stack (vault default)
Single self-contained `.html`, one `<style>`, vanilla JS, no build/framework/runtime deps, 0 `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, CDN/Bunny fonts. **Inline crisp `<svg>` icons — never a font, never emoji-as-icon, and (overriding Taste) never a runtime icon library.** Content in HTML so it renders JS-off.

## 3. Typography
Display: tracking −.02…−.04em, leading ~1.0, oversized `clamp()`. Body: 1.5–1.6, ~65ch, muted. **Sans-display is default** (Poppins/Outfit/Cabinet Grotesk/Geist/PP Neue Montreal); Inter = neutral fallback, not the reflexive pick. **Serif only** if the brief names it or it's genuinely editorial/luxury; **Fraunces & Instrument Serif banned as defaults.** Emphasis = italic/bold of the SAME family. Italic descenders (y g j p q): leading ≥1.1 + reserve padding.

## 4. Colour
Max 1 accent, saturation <80%. **Lila rule:** no default AI-purple/blue glow, no neon gradients. **Consistency lock:** one accent, whole page. Premium-consumer beige+brass+espresso banned as default.

## 5. Layout diversification (highest-value)
Anti-center bias when variance>4 (split/asymmetric/pinned). **Repetition ban:** each layout family ≤1×; 8 sections → ≥4 families. **Zigzag cap** ≤2 consecutive image+text. **EYEBROW RESTRAINT:** ≤1 eyebrow per 3 sections. **Split-header ban** unless right col carries a real visual. **Bento:** cells = content (no empty tiles), ≥2–3 cells with real visual variation.

## 6. Hero discipline
Fits viewport; headline ≤2 lines; subtext ≤20 words/≤4 lines; CTAs visible. **Hero stack ≤4 text elements**; trust/logo wall lives UNDER the hero. Font-size ↔ asset-size planned together.

## 7. Navigation
Single line desktop (condense/hamburger); height ≤80px.

## 8. Materiality
Cards only for real hierarchy; else border-top/dividers/whitespace. Shadows tinted to bg hue. **Shape-consistency lock:** one radius scale page-wide (or documented per-role).

## 9. Component quality
Comparison ✓/✗ per option (highlight "your" column). Pricing header-band + big price + CTA-per-card + featured tier. Roster avatar+tags+stats. **States (never success-only):** skeleton loaders, empty, error, tactile `:active`. **Button contrast AA**; CTA one line ≤3 words; **no duplicate CTA intent** (one label per intent). Forms: label above, error below, never placeholder-as-label, AA.

## 10. Motion (vanilla)
**"Motion claimed, motion shown"** (dial>4 must actually move). CSS transitions/animations, `IntersectionObserver` reveal, CSS `animation-timeline: view()` where supported. **Ban `window.addEventListener('scroll')` for per-frame work.** `prefers-reduced-motion` mandatory. Animate transform/opacity only; grain on fixed pointer-events:none pseudo; z-index restraint.

## 11. Images & content
Prefer REAL assets (crop from provided designs / brand folders). **Div fake-screenshots and text+gradient-blob heroes banned.** Complex hand-rolled illustration discouraged (simple marks OK). Logo walls = logos only. Density: headline ≤8 words + sub ≤25 + one asset/CTA; long lists→grouped/card/tabs/marquee. **Copy self-audit** before ship (kill broken grammar / cute AI wordplay; plain functional copy). Fake-precise numbers banned unless real/mock. Testimonials ≤3 lines, name+role+company, curly quotes, no em-dash flourish.

## 12. Non-negotiables + PRE-FLIGHT gate
Every clickable → a real designed page (no `href="#"` dead ends). Light/dark parity. **Pre-Flight (all pass):** eyebrows ≤ ceil(sections/3) · ≥4 layout families · ≤2 zigzags · one accent · one radius scale · CTAs one line & no duplicate intent · hero ≤4 elements & fits · vector icons · `node --check` clean · 0 browser storage · responsive 380/760/1200 · JS-off render · tag/`<div>` balance verified · **RENDER GATE passed** (rendered in the connected browser, screenshotted, visually inspected — fills canvas, no overflow/overlap/clipping).

## 13. PARITY GATE
Change spans >1 file/brand → (1) write the scope set; (2) build once, apply to every file in one pass; (3) parity table component×file, any `—` blocks; (4) verify the HTML element per file; (5) done = all green, log it.

## 14–16. Component-library upkeep · pods · after-round
Update `_COMPONENT-LIBRARY.md`; Studio Director → pods + Shared Services own the parity gate; log every round in the record/session loop.

---

# 17. DESIGN-SYSTEM & RESOURCE ARSENAL  (pull from MANY, re-implement to tokens, self-contained)
*Everything here is a **reference**, never a runtime dependency. Lift the token taxonomy / markup pattern / easing / SVG, then rebuild against the project's own tokens. Verify licences before commercial use.*

**A · Design systems with tokens** — Material 3 · Fluent 2 · Carbon · **Atlassian** (deepest public token naming) · Spectrum 2 · Primer · **Radix Colors** · **Open Props**. ⚠️ Polaris = Shopify only. Reverse-engineer: **getdesign.md** · **UIDrop**.

**B · Component libraries** — **daisyUI** (first pick) · **HyperUI** · React Bits · Skiper UI · Magic UI · Aceternity · shadcn/ui (Base UI default) · coss ui · Preline · **Flowbite** · 21st.dev · **HeroUI v3** (Apache-2.0) · Tailwind Plus · **404 Animation Library** · FeralUI. Headless: Base UI · Radix · React Aria · Ark · Headless UI. ⚠️ Vengeance UI never touch its token; Animmaster reference-only.

**C · Motion** — **GSAP** (100% free, first pick) · **Motion** · Anime.js v4 · **Lenis** · **Native CSS** scroll-driven. ⚠️ AOS stale.

**D · Icons (inline the SVG)** — **Lucide** (default) · Phosphor · **Tabler** (largest, MIT) · Heroicons · Remix · Iconoir · Material Symbols. Logos: logos.lndev.me · Simple Icons (CC0) · SVGL.

**E · Type** — **Fontshare** (Satoshi/Clash/General Sans) · Google Fonts (GDPR risk EU) · **Bunny Fonts** (EU) · Fontsource · UNCUT.wtf. **Arabic:** Amiri + Reem Kufi (set the face explicitly, check its line-height). *Never set a wireframe in Arial.*

**F · Colour & a11y (AA both themes)** — OKLCH picker · Adobe Leonardo · Radix Colors · WebAIM/APCA · WhoCanUse · Realtime Colors · Huemint.

**G · Texture / gradient / illustration** — **MagicPattern CSS backgrounds** · fffuel + **nnnoise** · Grainy-Gradients · **Haikei** · Josh Comeau gradient gen · Hero Patterns (CC BY) · **unDraw** · Humaaans (CC0) · ⚠️ Storyset (attribution) · Unsplash/Pexels.

**H · Inspiration** — Awwwards · CSS Design Awards · **Recent** · **One Page Love** · Minimal Gallery · SiteInspire · Lapa Ninja · Land-book.

**I · Generative media & 3D** — **three.js** r128 via Cloudflare CDN (no OrbitControls/CapsuleGeometry on that CDN; use Cylinder/Sphere; static fallback) · Devini Vault · ReelStack · MuAPI · Z-Image Turbo. ⚠️ TRELLIS 2 research-only.

**J · Build-free helpers** — Tailwind browser CDN (dev-only) · GRIGOLETTO Figma pack.

# 18. Choosing a direction — never default to one system
- **Project pins a system** (in its `CLAUDE.md`) → use it, don't deviate, don't ask.
- **Nothing pinned → deliver 2–3 genuinely distinct directions** from *different rows of the arsenal*. Each = **the same page built for real** in single-file HTML; each declares its sources; one paragraph each on what it signals / where it wins / where it fights. **Ahmed picks; write the winner into that project's `CLAUDE.md`.**
- **Go beyond:** **mix** token taxonomy from one, component pattern from a second, motion from a third, icons/type from others — always re-implemented to the project's own tokens, self-contained.

# 19. Licence traps & standing rules (binding)
Logo sets ≠ trademark licences. Attribution: Storyset, Hero Patterns (CC BY). React Bits = MIT + Commons Clause (no resale). HeroUI v3 = Apache-2.0 (carry NOTICE). Polaris = Shopify-only. Tabler SVGs MIT. Google Fonts hotlink = GDPR → Bunny. TRELLIS 2 research-only. Animmaster reference-only. **Never recommend SellTheMethod. Vengeance UI code fine, never its token. Use Hyperframes not Cantina. Use `opencut-classic` not OpenCut main.**

*Corrections vs stale memory: GSAP fully free · shadcn default primitive Radix→Base UI · HeroUI MIT→Apache-2.0 · Origin UI→coss · Godly→Recent · Get Waves→Haikei.*

11 Resources/skills/senior-build-inspect.text:
---
name: "senior-build-inspection"
description: "When a website is important (client-facing, revenue-driving, high-traffic, brand- or legally-critical), have senior full-stack and backend engineers inspect the finished build and issue a signed Build Receipt Report — documenting the exact page/route structure and the stack it's developed with, plus an engineering assessment (architecture, performance, security, data/backend, deployment, accessibility) and a Ship / Fix-first verdict. Triggers on: \"important/critical website\", pre-ship or pre-launch engineering review, \"inspect the build\", \"issue a receipt/report\", \"what stack is this built with\", senior sign-off, backend/full-stack audit, before go-live."
---

# Senior Build Inspection — the Build Receipt Report

A quality gate for **websites that matter**. Before an important site ships, **senior full-stack and backend engineers** inspect the finished build and issue a **Build Receipt Report**: a signed, dated record of *what was built* (page/route structure), *how it's built* (the stack), and *whether it's safe to launch*.

This is not the design review (that's the three-directions / frontend gate) and not the light QA pass. It is the **senior engineering sign-off** — the receipt the Owner keeps as proof the build was inspected by experienced engineers.

---

## 1. When to run — the importance test

Run this gate when **any** of these is true:
- The site is **client-facing** or represents the brand publicly.
- It **drives revenue** (e-commerce, lead-gen, bookings, payments).
- It expects **meaningful traffic** or must stay up (SLA / reputation).
- It handles **personal data, auth, or money** (legal / security exposure).
- It's **brand- or legally-critical** (a flagship, a launch, a regulated space).

If none apply (a throwaway wireframe, an internal sketch), skip — a light QA pass is enough. **When in doubt, treat it as important and run the gate.**

## 2. Who inspects

Assign **two named seniors**, and record their names in the report:
- **Senior Full-Stack Engineer** — owns the whole picture: page/route structure, front-to-back data flow, integration correctness, build integrity.
- **Senior Backend Engineer** — owns the server side: APIs, data model, auth, security, performance, deployment, reliability.

For a static single-file site with no backend, the Full-Stack lead still runs the structural + delivery checks and notes "no backend" explicitly in the stack manifest.

## 3. What they produce — the Build Receipt Report

A comprehensive long-form document (house standard: Arial `.docx` + `.pdf`, cover page, navigable contents), filed under the project name. It contains, in order:

**A. Header / receipt block** — project name, URL/build path, version/commit, date, the two inspecting engineers, and the final **Verdict** (Ship ✓ / Ship with follow-ups / Fix-first ✗).

**B. Page & route structure** — the receipt of *what exists*. Enumerate **every page/route**; for each: its purpose, the **sections/blocks** it contains, key components, internal links in/out, and load method (static, SSR, CSR, prerendered). Present as a route map/tree so nothing is undocumented. Flag orphan pages, dead links, and duplicated structure.

**C. Stack manifest** — the receipt of *how it's built*. Document the **exact stack the site is developed with**:
- **Frontend** — language, framework/library (or "vanilla single-file HTML"), CSS approach, build tool, key dependencies + versions, fonts/icons/assets and their licences.
- **Backend** — runtime/language, framework, APIs/endpoints, business logic location.
- **Data** — database(s), schema shape, ORM, migrations, caching.
- **Auth & payments** — provider, session model, token handling (never record secrets).
- **Hosting / deployment** — host, CDN, domain/DNS, CI/CD, environment config.
- **Third-party** — analytics, connectors, external services.
Note anything **unknown or unverifiable** rather than guessing.

**D. Engineering assessment** — the seniors' judgement across:
- **Architecture** — is the structure sound, maintainable, and matched to the site's importance? Over/under-engineered?
- **Performance** — payload size, render path, images, caching, Core Web Vitals risks.
- **Security** — input handling, auth, secrets, dependency risk, headers, common web vulnerabilities; extra scrutiny if data/money/auth are involved.
- **Data & backend** — schema integrity, query safety, error handling, rate limits, backups.
- **Deployment & reliability** — reproducible build, rollback, monitoring, uptime posture.
- **Accessibility & standards** — WCAG AA in both themes, semantics, JS-off behaviour.

**E. Findings** — a prioritised list: **Blocker** (must fix before launch) · **Major** (fix soon) · **Minor** (polish). Each finding: what, where, why it matters, recommended fix.

**F. Verdict & sign-off** — one of:
- **Ship ✓** — no blockers; safe to launch.
- **Ship with follow-ups** — launch allowed; listed majors scheduled.
- **Fix-first ✗** — blockers present; do not launch until cleared, then re-inspect.
Signed by both engineers, dated. Owner-reserved go-live decisions (spending money, going public, accepting legal terms) **escalate to the human Principal (NeedHuman)** — the engineers advise, the Owner decides.

## 4. How to inspect (method)

1. **Confirm importance** (§1) and record why it qualifies.
2. **Read the actual build** — open the files/repo; do not infer from the brief. Walk every route; read the real source, config, and any backend.
3. **Reconstruct the structure and stack from evidence** — enumerate routes/sections; identify frameworks/deps/hosting from the code and config, not assumptions. Mark unverifiable items as such.
4. **Run the assessment** (§3D) — check, don't assume; where tooling exists (build check, link check, Lighthouse-style pass, dependency audit), use it and cite results.
5. **Write findings and verdict**, then **build the report** (Arial docx + pdf), file it under the project, and log the inspection in the request log with the two engineers named.

## 5. Rules

- **Evidence over assumption.** Every structural and stack claim traces to the real build. If it can't be verified, say so.
- **Two seniors, both named.** No anonymous sign-off.
- **Blockers block.** A Fix-first verdict means the site does not go live until re-inspected.
- **Never record secrets** (keys, tokens, passwords, DB creds) in the report — reference their existence and handling only.
- **The receipt is kept.** The report is the Owner's proof of inspection; archive superseded versions, never delete.
- **Human decides go-live.** Engineers recommend; publishing/purchasing/legal acceptance is the Owner's call (NeedHuman).

## 6. Fit with the Fish Code process

> Request → design gate (three-directions) → build → Checkup & Validation → **[if important] Senior Build Inspection → Build Receipt Report** → Owner go-live decision → deliver + pin + log

This gate sits **after** the build and standard validation and **before** go-live, only for sites that pass the importance test. It complements — does not replace — the design and frontend QA passes.

11 Resources/skills/visual-self-verify/S.text:
---
name: "visual-self-verify"
description: "Render-and-verify loop for any visual you build (HTML page, social post, carousel slide, SVG, component) BEFORE showing it to the user. Use whenever you produce a fixed-size visual and cannot trust un-rendered markup — it opens the file in the user's connected Chrome, screenshots it, and checks layout so you never ship blind. Triggers on: built a page/post/slide, \"does this render\", verify the design, screenshot my output, check the layout, why does it look broken, self-verify, render gate."
---

# Visual Self-Verify — render your own output and look at it before delivery

**Core rule: never present a visual you have not rendered and inspected.** Un-rendered HTML/SVG hides overflow, dead space, overlaps, clipped text, mis-placed connectors and un-rendered icons. Render → look → fix → repeat until clean. Only then present.

## Why not a headless browser
This sandbox has **no** working headless browser: Chromium downloads are blocked and `playwright install-deps` fails (no sudo). Do **not** burn time retrying those. Use the **user's connected Chrome** via the `claude-in-chrome` MCP instead.

## The loop (fast, ~1 screenshot per iteration)

1. **Confirm a browser is connected:** `list_connected_browsers`. If none, ask the user to connect the Chrome extension.
2. **Get a tab:** `tabs_create_mcp` (or reuse one), then keep its `tabId`.
3. **Navigate to a real origin:** `navigate` the tab to `https://example.com`. (The navigate tool prepends `https://` and rejects long `data:`/`file://` URLs, so you cannot navigate straight to the file — you inject instead.)
4. **Compress the file in the shell** so the inject payload stays small:
   `python3 -c "import gzip,base64;print(base64.b64encode(gzip.compress(open('FILE.html','rb').read())).decode())"`
5. **Inject + fit + (optionally) screenshot in one `browser_batch`.** Run `javascript_tool` with:
   ```js
   var b='<PASTE_GZIP_BASE64>';
   var bin=Uint8Array.from(atob(b),c=>c.charCodeAt(0));
   var html=await new Response(new Blob([bin]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip'))).text();
   document.open();document.write(html);document.close();
   document.documentElement.style.zoom='0.5';           // fit a tall canvas into one screenshot
   document.body.style.alignItems='flex-start';          // stop flex-centering hiding the top
   'ok';
   ```
   Then `computer{action:screenshot, tabId}`. If it returns `CDP ... captureScreenshot timed out`, just call screenshot again once — the renderer was mid-paint.
6. **Inspect the screenshot honestly**, checking:
   - content **fills the canvas** — no big empty/dead zone, nothing floating in a void;
   - **no overflow / overlap** — sections don't collide, nothing spills past the frame;
   - **connectors/arrows/streams land where intended**;
   - **text not clipped**, headlines fit, no `…` truncation you didn't intend;
   - **icons / illustrations actually render** (not empty boxes);
   - **contrast holds** (legible in both themes if relevant).
7. **Zoom for detail:** `computer{action:zoom, region:[x0,y0,x1,y1], tabId}` (region is corners, x1>x0, y1>y0) to read small text or check an arrowhead.
8. **Fix the generator/file, re-run steps 4–7** until clean.
9. **Close the tab** (`tabs_close_mcp`) when done.

## Notes
- **Animated posts:** a single screenshot can't show motion — render the **static twin** (final-frame version, animations disabled) to verify the *layout*, then trust the shared motion code for the animated one.
- **Fixed-size canvases** (e.g. 1080×1440 social posts): the `zoom` + `flex-start` step is what lets the whole canvas land in one frame; drop zoom to ~0.37 to see an entire very-tall canvas, raise toward 0.6 to read text.
- **Tool loading:** if these tools are deferred, load them in one `ToolSearch`: `select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__list_connected_browsers,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch`.
- **Keep payloads small:** always gzip before base64; a raw base64 of a large file can exceed argument limits and wastes context.
- This is the same **RENDER GATE** referenced by `ultimate-frontend-uiux` §0.7 / §12 — run it as the final step before any visual deliverable.

11 Resources/skills/transcribe-voice-not.text:
---
name: transcribe-voice-notes
description: Turn voice notes and audio messages into readable, searchable, citable text — WhatsApp exports (_chat.txt plus .opus files), Telegram/Signal exports, or any folder of .opus/.m4a/.ogg/.mp3/.wav recordings. Produces a per-file transcript, a merged chat log with each voice note inlined in conversation order, and a CSV index. Use this skill WHENEVER the user mentions voice notes, voice messages, audio messages, WhatsApp exports, "listen to these recordings", "what did he say in the voice note", transcribing audio, or needs audio turned into evidence, minutes, a chronology or an exhibit bundle — even if they never say the word "transcribe". Also use it when a transcription attempt has already failed for lack of a model: this skill carries the offline / bring-your-own-weights route and a no-ASR fallback that still makes a large voice-note archive usable.
---

# Transcribe voice notes

Voice notes are the least searchable evidence anyone owns and usually the most
important. This skill turns a pile of them into text you can read, search, quote
and cite — and, when no speech model is reachable, still turns it into something
navigable rather than fifteen hours of silence.

**Never send audio to a third-party web transcription service.** Voice notes are
routinely privileged, confidential or personal. Everything here runs locally. If
no local route exists, use the fallback in Step 4 and say so plainly — do not
substitute an online service, and do not offer one.

---

## Step 1 — Always index first (30 seconds, never fails)

Before any transcription, build the index. It is cheap, it works with no model,
and it is what makes the transcript usable afterwards.

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_index.py "<export folder>" --out-dir ./vn
```

This writes `vn/voice_index.csv` — one row per voice note with date, time,
sender, duration estimate, file name, and **the surrounding text messages**. For
a WhatsApp export it reads `_chat.txt` so each note is anchored in its
conversation.

Add `--rank` with topic keywords to produce `vn/listen_list.md`, a scored
shortlist:

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_index.py "<export folder>" --out-dir ./vn --rank \
  --topic "remote work:remote,عن بعد,from home" \
  --topic "pay:salary,راتب,allowance" \
  --window 2024-10:2025-01:6
```

`--window START:END:BONUS` adds score to notes falling inside a date range —
use it for the period the matter actually turns on.

## Step 2 — Decide *where* it runs, then choose a route

Audio is expensive to move; a model file is cheap to move once. If the voice
notes sit on the user's machine and that machine has python and ffmpeg, run
there and transfer nothing. See `references/agent-driven-runs.md` — it also
carries the batch loop for driving a long job from a shell that dies after
about a minute.

## Step 2b — Choose a transcription route

Run the probe. It reports every route available on this machine and picks one.

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_transcribe.py --routes
```

Routes, best first:

| Route | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `faster-whisper` | `pip install faster-whisper` + local weights | Fastest on CPU; int8 quantisation; best default |
| `whisper.cpp` | `whisper-cli` (or `main`) binary + a `ggml-*.bin` | Excellent on Apple Silicon; single self-contained file |
| `openai-whisper` | `pip install openai-whisper` + weights | Slowest, most memory, widest language support |
| `platform` | macOS `speech-to-text` / Windows Speech / `sox`+local engine | Only if already configured |
| *(none)* | — | Go to Step 4 |

**Weights are the usual blocker, not the software.** In locked-down
environments the package installs fine and the model download is refused with
`403`. Diagnose and fix it with the setup helper rather than guessing:

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_setup.py --check                    # what's here, what's reachable
python3 scripts/vn_setup.py --plan medium --route whisper.cpp
python3 scripts/vn_setup.py --verify /models/ggml-medium.bin
python3 scripts/vn_setup.py --selftest /models/ggml-medium.bin --sample note.opus
```

`--plan` prints the exact file to fetch, on any machine with ordinary internet,
and where to put it. `--assemble` rebuilds a model that had to be split to move
it. `--verify` catches the classic failure where an HTML error page was saved
under the model's filename. One download, then permanently offline. Read
`references/models-offline.md` before ever telling a user transcription is
impossible.

## Step 3 — Transcribe in batches, with resume

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_transcribe.py "<export folder>" --out-dir ./vn \
  --model-path /path/to/model --language auto --batch 50 --max-seconds 0
```

- Writes one JSON per file into `vn/transcripts/`, and appends to a
  `vn/ledger.jsonl`. **Re-running skips anything already in the ledger**, so a
  long job survives interruption — always safe to run again.
- `--only-list vn/listen_list.md` transcribes just the shortlist. On a large
  archive, do this first and show the user results before committing hours.
- `--language auto` detects per file. For Arabic dialects pass
  `--language ar --prompt "<a few names and terms that appear>"` — a short
  vocabulary prompt materially improves proper nouns.
- `--max-seconds N` stops cleanly before a short shell timeout kills the
  process. Essential when driving this remotely — see
  `references/agent-driven-runs.md`.
- Report progress honestly: files done, minutes of audio done, estimated
  remaining. Never imply a finished archive when a batch is running.

Then merge back into conversation order:

```bash
python3 scripts/vn_merge.py "<export folder>" --out-dir ./vn
```

`vn/chat_with_transcripts.md` is the deliverable — the original chat log with
every voice note replaced by `🎤 [1m38s] transcript text…`, so it reads as one
continuous conversation.

## Step 4 — When no model is reachable

Do not stop and do not improvise an online service. Do this instead, and be
explicit with the user about what is and is not possible:

1. **Deliver the index and the ranked listen list.** Fifteen hours of audio
   becomes a shortlist of twenty the user can work through in an evening.
2. **Point them at transcription they already own** — WhatsApp transcribes voice
   notes on the phone (long-press → Transcribe); iOS and Android both have
   on-device dictation. These are local and free.
3. **Offer the offline route** in `references/models-offline.md`: one download on
   any machine with internet, dropped into a folder, and this skill works
   permanently offline thereafter.
4. **Take dictation back.** When the user listens and tells you what was said,
   record it in `vn/manual_transcripts.csv` (same columns as the index) and
   `vn_merge.py` will fold it in exactly like a machine transcript.

## Step 5 — Verify before relying on it

Transcripts are evidence-adjacent; treat them as drafts.

- Spot-check the highest-value notes against the audio, or ask the user to.
- Mark every transcript `[machine transcript — unverified]` unless a human has
  confirmed it. Keep that marker in any document that quotes it.
- Never quote a machine transcript as a verbatim admission in a document that
  goes to a third party without the user confirming the wording first.
- Where the model's confidence is low, the JSON carries it — surface it rather
  than smoothing the text.

## Output contract

```
vn/
├── voice_index.csv            every note + context (always)
├── listen_list.md             ranked shortlist (with --rank)
├── transcripts/*.json         one per file, with segments and confidence
```

---
name: docx
description: "Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation."
license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
---

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)

---
name: pdf
description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
---

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs
```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata
```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout
```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text()
        print(text)
```

#### Extract Tables
```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
            for row in table:
                print(row)
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction
```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

## Command-Line Tools

### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
```bash
# Extract text
pdftotext input.pdf output.txt

# Extract text preserving layout
pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt

# Extract specific pages
pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
```

### qpdf
```bash
# Merge PDFs
qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf

# Split pages
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf

# Rotate pages
qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees

# Remove password
qpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
```

### pdftk (if available)
```bash
# Merge
pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Split
pdftk input.pdf burst

# Rotate
pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
```

## Common Tasks

### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
```python
# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
import pytesseract
from pdf2image import convert_from_path

# Convert PDF to images
images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')

# OCR each page
text = ""
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
    text += "\n\n"

print(text)
```

### Add Watermark
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### Extract Images
```bash
# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix

# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
```

### Password Protection
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    writer.add_page(page)

# Add password
writer.encrypt("userpassword", "ownerpassword")

with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

## Quick Reference

| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |

## Next Steps

- For advanced pypdfium2 usage, see REFERENCE.md
- For JavaScript libraries (pdf-lib), see REFERENCE.md
- If you need to fill out a PDF form, follow the instructions in FORMS.md
- For troubleshooting guides, see REFERENCE.md

---
name: pptx
description: "Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill."
license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
---

# PPTX creation, editing, and analysis

If this session offers a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill, and the user has neither asked for a PowerPoint/.pptx file nor supplied a .pptx/.potx file, build the deck with that type or skill instead; this skill remains the right tool for producing .pptx files and for reading, editing, templating, or converting existing .pptx/.potx files.

A `.pptx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new deck | Write a `pptxgenjs` script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing deck, or build from a template | unzip → edit `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` → zip |
| **Read** content | `markitdown deck.pptx` (one block per slide under `<!-- Slide number: N -->` markers); visual grid: `python scripts/thumbnail.py deck.pptx` |

## Scripts

Paths are relative to this skill's directory. Everything else is plain Python, `node`, or shell.

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/thumbnail.py deck.pptx [prefix]` | Labeled grid of every slide, for picking template layouts. `.pptx` only. Pass `prefix` — it defaults to `thumbnails`, which overwrites the grids of any other deck done in the same directory |
| `scripts/add_slide.py unpacked/ slide2.xml [--after slideN.xml]` | Duplicate a slide (or a `slideLayoutN.xml`) with all the package bookkeeping. Also takes a `.pptx` directly with `-o out.pptx` |
| `scripts/clean.py unpacked/` | Delete slides, media, and rels no longer referenced. Run **after** `<p:sldIdLst>` is final |
| `scripts/office/validate.py deck.pptx [--original src.pptx]` | Schema, relationship, content-type, chart and slide checks; each failure names its fix. Pass `--original` for any template-derived deck — it baselines the schema checks against the template, so the template's own XSD errors don't read as yours |
| `scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf deck.pptx` | LibreOffice wrapper — bare `soffice` hangs in this sandbox |

## Creating with pptxgenjs — gotchas

`pptxgenjs` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('pptxgenjs')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install pptxgenjs`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Set `pres.layout` before adding slides.** The default canvas is `LAYOUT_16x9` = **10" × 5.625"**, not 13.3" wide. Coordinates past the edge are written, not clamped — the shape just isn't on the slide. (`LAYOUT_WIDE` is 13.3" × 7.5".)
- **Hex colors: never `#`, never 8 digits.** `color: "FF0000"`. Both `"#FF0000"` and alpha baked into the hex (`"00000020"`) **corrupt the file**. For translucency: `transparency: 0-100` on fills and images, `opacity: 0.0-1.0` on shadows — each is silently ignored on the other.
- **pptxgenjs mutates option objects in place** (converts values to EMU on first use). Never share one `shadow`/options object across two `add*` calls — build a fresh object each time.
- **Shadow `offset` must be ≥ 0** — a negative offset corrupts the file. To cast a shadow upward, use `angle: 270` with a positive offset.
- **`letterSpacing` is silently ignored** — the real option is `charSpacing`.
- **Lists:** `bullet: true` on each item, never a literal `•` (renders double bullets). Set `breakLine: true` on every array item except the last. Space bulleted paragraphs with `paraSpaceAfter`, not `lineSpacing` (huge gaps).
- **One `new pptxgen()` per output file** — never reuse an instance.
- **`rectRadius` only works on `ROUNDED_RECTANGLE`**, not `RECTANGLE`.
- **Gradient fills aren't supported** — use a gradient image as the background instead.
- **Every `addText` call needs `isTextBox: true`** — without it the shape lacks `txBox="1"`, so screen readers announce the text as a "graphic" instead of a text box. No visual change.
- **Text boxes have built-in internal padding** — set `margin: 0` whenever text must align with a shape, line, or icon at the same x.
- **Speaker notes go in `slide.addNotes("...")`** (plain text, once per slide), never in a text box on the slide.
- **Keep charts native.** Use `addChart()` for everything PowerPoint can chart (pass an array of `{type, data, options}` for combos). For PowerPoint-native features the library doesn't expose (trendlines, error bars), compute the extra series yourself or post-process the generated OOXML — do not fall back to a rendered image. Only chart types PowerPoint has no native form for (Sankey, network, chord) go in as images.
- **Default charts render bare** — no title, no data labels, dated palette. Set `showTitle` + `title`, `showValue: true` + `dataLabelPosition`, `chartColors: [...]` from your palette, and quiet the frame (`catAxisLabelColor`/`valAxisLabelColor`, `valGridLine: { color, size }`, `catGridLine: { style: "none" }`, `showLegend: false` for a single series).
- **On a stacked bar or column chart, `dataLabelPosition` must be `ctr`, `inEnd`, or `inBase`.** `outEnd` **corrupts the file**.
- **A combo series using `secondaryValAxis`/`secondaryCatAxis` needs both `valAxes` and `catAxes` on the chart options, two entries each.** Without them pptxgenjs writes axis *ids* it never declares, and PowerPoint **discards that chart** and reports the file as corrupt. Supplying only `valAxes` is not enough.
- **After `writeFile()`, run `python scripts/office/validate.py deck.pptx`.** It reports the two chart faults above and the slide-XML defects PowerPoint refuses, and names the fix for each. Fix them in your generator, not by hand-editing the packed XML.
- **Never reorder the children of `<p:presentation>`.** pptxgenjs writes `<p:notesMasterIdLst>` right after `<p:sldIdLst>` and points both masters at one theme part. PowerPoint reads that happily — move the element and the same deck becomes unopenable.
- **Icons:** render `react-icons` to SVG (`ReactDOMServer.renderToStaticMarkup`), rasterize with `sharp` at ≥256px, and insert via `addImage({ data: "image/png;base64," + buf.toString("base64") })` — the `image/png;base64,` prefix is required (`react-icons`, `react`, `react-dom`, and `sharp` are preinstalled — `npm install react-icons react react-dom sharp` only if a require fails).

## Editing existing decks and templates

Pick layouts first: `python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx template-thumbs` writes a labeled grid of every slide and prints the file(s) it created — `template-thumbs.jpg`, split into `template-thumbs-N.jpg` past 12 slides. **Always pass that second argument, named after the deck.** It defaults to `thumbnails`, so two decks thumbnailed in one directory silently overwrite each other's grids — the first deck's are simply gone (template analysis only — visual QA needs the full-resolution renders from [Converting to Images](#converting-to-images); it only accepts `.pptx`, so copy a `.potx` to a `.pptx` name first). Use it with `markitdown` to map each content section onto a template slide, and vary the layouts — don't put every section on the same title-and-bullets slide.

```bash
python3 -c "import sys,zipfile; zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall('unpacked')" deck.pptx
python scripts/add_slide.py unpacked/ slide2.xml --after slide2.xml   # duplicate a slide (or slideLayoutN.xml); prints the new slide's path
# reorder / delete slides = edit <p:sldIdLst> in ppt/presentation.xml
python scripts/clean.py unpacked/                                     # after deletions: removes orphaned slides, media, rels
# edit slide content in ppt/slides/slideN.xml
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.pptx && zip -Xr ../out.pptx .)           # zip from INSIDE the dir; rm first or deleted parts survive
python scripts/office/validate.py out.pptx --original deck.pptx
```

- **Do all structural work — add, delete, reorder — before editing any slide's content.** `add_slide.py` copies a slide file verbatim, so duplicating after you edit clones the edited content; and `clean.py` deletes any slide missing from `<p:sldIdLst>`, including one you just wrote.
- **Never copy a slide file by hand** — `add_slide.py` does every registration a new slide needs and reports what it made (`Created ppt/slides/slide17.xml from slide2.xml`). It also works directly on a file: `add_slide.py deck.pptx slide2.xml -o out.pptx` — **pass `-o`, or it rewrites the input deck in place.** A duplicated slide still *references* its source's chart/SmartArt/embedded-object parts rather than cloning them, so editing one slide's chart changes the other's.
- **If you use `python-pptx`**, three things it won't do: duplicate a slide (its only entry point is `add_slide(layout)`), preserve formatting through `text_frame.text = "..."` (that collapses the paragraph to a single unstyled run — assign `run.text` instead), or read the SVG/EMF most template art uses (`add_picture` raises `UnidentifiedImageError`).
- Legacy `.ppt` must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pptx file.ppt`. `.potx` templates unpack and pack identically — keep the `.potx` extension on the output.
- To reuse a template icon or image, duplicate a slide or layout that already contains it.

When filling in a template:

- If you script an XML transform, parse with `defusedxml.minidom` — round-tripping OOXML through `xml.etree.ElementTree` rewrites namespace prefixes and corrupts the deck.
- **Template slots ≠ source items.** If the template shows 4 team members and you have 3, delete the 4th member's entire group (image + text boxes), not just its text — then check for orphaned visuals in QA.
- One `<a:p>` per list item — never concatenate items into a single paragraph. Copy the sibling `<a:pPr>` to preserve spacing, and put `b="1"` on the `<a:rPr>` of titles, section headers, and inline labels (`Status:`, `Owner:`).
- Let bullets inherit from the layout; only add `<a:buChar>`, `<a:buAutoNum>` (numbered), or `<a:buNone>` to override — never a literal `•` in the text.
- Text with leading or trailing spaces needs `xml:space="preserve"` on its `<a:t>`.

## Design Ideas

**Don't create boring slides.** Plain bullets on a white background won't impress anyone. Consider ideas from this list for each slide.

### Before Starting

- **Pick a bold, content-informed color palette**: The palette should feel designed for THIS topic. If swapping your colors into a completely different presentation would still "work," you haven't made specific enough choices.
- **Dominance over equality**: One color should dominate (60-70% visual weight), with 1-2 supporting tones and one sharp accent. Never give all colors equal weight.
- **Dark/light contrast**: Dark backgrounds for title + conclusion slides, light for content ("sandwich" structure). Or commit to dark throughout for a premium feel.
- **Commit to a visual motif**: Pick ONE distinctive element and repeat it — rounded image frames, icons in colored circles. Carry it across every slide. **Do not use a color bar or accent stripe as your motif** (see Avoid list).

### Color Palettes

Choose colors that match your topic — don't default to generic blue. Use these palettes as inspiration:

| Theme | Primary | Secondary | Accent |
|-------|---------|-----------|--------|
| **Midnight Executive** | `1E2761` (navy) | `CADCFC` (ice blue) | `FFFFFF` (white) |
| **Forest & Moss** | `2C5F2D` (forest) | `97BC62` (moss) | `F5F5F5` (cream) |
| **Coral Energy** | `F96167` (coral) | `F9E795` (gold) | `2F3C7E` (navy) |
| **Warm Terracotta** | `B85042` (terracotta) | `E7E8D1` (sand) | `A7BEAE` (sage) |
| **Ocean Gradient** | `065A82` (deep blue) | `1C7293` (teal) | `21295C` (midnight) |
| **Charcoal Minimal** | `36454F` (charcoal) | `F2F2F2` (off-white) | `212121` (black) |
| **Teal Trust** | `028090` (teal) | `00A896` (seafoam) | `02C39A` (mint) |
| **Berry & Cream** | `6D2E46` (berry) | `A26769` (dusty rose) | `ECE2D0` (cream) |
| **Sage Calm** | `84B59F` (sage) | `69A297` (eucalyptus) | `50808E` (slate) |
| **Cherry Bold** | `990011` (cherry) | `FCF6F5` (off-white) | `2F3C7E` (navy) |

### For Each Slide

**Every slide needs a visual element** — image, chart, icon, or shape. Text-only slides are forgettable.

**Layout options:**
- Two-column (text left, illustration on right)
- Icon + text rows (icon in colored circle, bold header, description below)
- 2x2 or 2x3 grid (image on one side, grid of content blocks on other)
- Half-bleed image (full left or right side) with content overlay

**Data display:**
- Large stat callouts (big numbers 60-72pt with small labels below)
- Comparison columns (before/after, pros/cons, side-by-side options)
- Timeline or process flow (numbered steps, arrows)

**Visual polish:**
- Icons in small colored circles next to section headers
- Italic accent text for key stats or taglines

### Typography

**Font names you write into the .pptx are rendered by the user's PowerPoint, not by this environment.** Your visual QA renders via LibreOffice, which substitutes fonts it doesn't have — and for some fonts the substitute has different widths, so your QA preview can show text overflow (or fit) that the real deck won't have. To keep your QA trustworthy:

- **Safe fonts** (render true-to-width in QA *and* ship with Office): **Arial, Calibri, Cambria, Times New Roman, Courier New, Bookman Old Style, Century Schoolbook**. Use these for body text and anything where fit matters.
- **Headers with personality at zero QA risk**: pair a safe-list serif header (Cambria, Bookman Old Style, Century Schoolbook) with a safe-list sans body (Calibri or Arial). You get visual contrast without giving up reliable overflow checks.
- **If the user asks for a font outside the safe list** (e.g. Georgia or Trebuchet MS): use it where the user asked, but size those containers with extra slack (~10%) and don't trust QA text-fit on those elements — the preview of that font is approximate. If the user hasn't specified, prefer safe-list fonts for body text.
- **QA-unreliable fonts** (substitute has different widths — overflow checks can be wrong): Georgia, Trebuchet MS, Impact, Arial Black, Garamond, Consolas, Palatino Linotype. Calibri Light substitution varies by environment; treat as QA-unreliable. Fine for titles/accents with slack; don't trust QA text-fit on these.
- **Never default to Aptos** — Office's post-2023 default has no metric-compatible substitute here *and* is missing from older Office installs, so it's unreliable on both ends.

| Element | Size |
|---------|------|
| Slide title | 36-44pt bold |
| Section header | 20-24pt bold |
| Body text | 14-16pt |
| Captions | 10-12pt muted |

### Spacing

- 0.5" minimum margins
- 0.3-0.5" between content blocks
- Leave breathing room—don't fill every inch

### Avoid (Common Mistakes)

- **Don't repeat the same layout** — vary columns, cards, and callouts across slides
- **Don't center body text** — left-align paragraphs and lists; center only titles
- **Don't skimp on size contrast** — titles need 36pt+ to stand out from 14-16pt body
- **Don't default to blue** — pick colors that reflect the specific topic
- **Don't mix spacing randomly** — choose 0.3" or 0.5" gaps and use consistently
- **Don't style one slide and leave the rest plain** — commit fully or keep it simple throughout
- **Don't create text-only slides** — add images, icons, charts, or visual elements; avoid plain title + bullets
- **Don't forget text box padding** — when aligning lines or shapes with text edges, set `margin: 0` on the text box or offset the shape to account for padding
- **Don't use low-contrast elements** — icons AND text need strong contrast against the background; avoid light text on light backgrounds or dark text on dark backgrounds
- **NEVER use accent lines under titles** — these are a hallmark of AI-generated slides; use whitespace or background color instead
- **NEVER add decorative color bars or accent stripes** — this includes: header/footer bars spanning the slide width, vertical sidebar stripes down one edge of the slide, thin accent stripes along one edge of a card or content block, and "single-side borders" on rectangles. These read as AI-generated filler. If you want to set a card apart, use a subtle background tint, a drop shadow, or an icon — not an edge stripe.
- **Don't default to cream/beige backgrounds** — when no background is specified, use white (`FFFFFF`) or the user's brand palette; avoid warm-neutral defaults like `F5F5DC`, `FAF0E6`, `FAEBD7`, `FFF8E1`
- **Don't ship text that overflows its shape** — if text doesn't fit, reduce font size, split across slides, or enlarge the container; never leave content cut off or spilling past bounds

## QA (Required)

Your first render usually has a few real issues — overlaps, overflow, misalignment. Find and fix those, re-render only the slides you changed, and stop.

### Content QA

```bash
markitdown output.pptx
```

Check for missing content, typos, wrong order.

**When using templates, check for leftover placeholder text:**

```bash
markitdown output.pptx | grep -iE "\bx{3,}\b|lorem|ipsum|\bTODO|\[insert|this.*(page|slide).*layout"
```

If grep returns results, fix them before declaring success.

### File QA (required)

```bash
python scripts/office/validate.py output.pptx                      # built from scratch
python scripts/office/validate.py output.pptx --original src.pptx  # built from a template
```

**If the deck came from a template, always pass `--original`.** A template may itself
contain parts the XSD rejects, so a bare run can report failures you never caused — and
a genuine regression can hide among them. `--original` baselines
the schema and slide checks against the template, suppressing errors it already had.
The structural checks — relationships, content types, charts — ignore `--original` and
report template-inherited problems either way, so read those on their own merits.

pptxgenjs emits chart XML PowerPoint refuses to open, and every other tool
accepts: python-pptx opens those decks, LibreOffice renders them, the XSD
passes them. Every failure names its fix. Fix it in the generator and rebuild.

### Visual QA

Convert the slides to images (see [Converting to Images](#converting-to-images)) and inspect every one. After staring at the generating code you tend to see what you expect rather than what rendered, so look at the images fresh (a subagent works well for this if you have one). User-visible defects to look for:

- **Text overflow or text cut off at a box or slide boundary — check this first.** It is the most common defect and always user-visible. (For a font the previewer renders unreliably per Typography, the preview is approximate: trust the ~10% slack you left, not its apparent fit.)
- Overlapping elements (text through shapes, lines through words, stacked elements)
- Source citations or footers colliding with content above
- Elements too close (< 0.3" gaps) or cards/sections nearly touching
- Uneven gaps (large empty area in one place, cramped in another)
- Insufficient margin from slide edges (< 0.5")
- Columns or similar elements not aligned consistently
- Low-contrast text (e.g., light gray text on cream-colored background)
- Template decoration mispositioned after text replacement — e.g., a title underline positioned for one line, but the replaced title wrapped to two
- Low-contrast icons (e.g., dark icons on dark backgrounds without a contrasting circle)
- Text boxes too narrow causing excessive wrapping
- Leftover placeholder content

## Converting to Images

Convert presentations to individual slide images for visual inspection:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.pptx
rm -f slide-*.jpg
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 output.pdf slide
ls -1 "$PWD"/slide-*.jpg
```

**Pass the absolute paths printed above directly to the view tool.** The `rm` clears stale images from prior runs. `pdftoppm` zero-pads based on page count: `slide-1.jpg` for decks under 10 pages, `slide-01.jpg` for 10-99, `slide-001.jpg` for 100+.

**After fixes, rerun all four commands above** — the PDF must be regenerated from the edited `.pptx` before `pdftoppm` can reflect your changes.

## Dependencies

`pptxgenjs` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('pptxgenjs')` fails) · `markitdown[pptx]`, `Pillow`, `defusedxml`, `lxml` (pip — text dump, thumbnail, clean, validate) · LibreOffice (`soffice`, auto-configured for sandboxed environments via `scripts/office/soffice.py`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)
